# Medical Privacy At Risk:
ImmTrac Consent Concerns
| |
---
|
---
Nearly a decade after first raising concerns about **Texas’ immunization registry** , TFVC is again sounding the alarm about ImmTrac. Texas law continues to **require voluntary enrollment** in ImmTrac with explicit, written parental or patient consent. TFVC has successfully helped block repeated legislative efforts to convert the system into automatic “opt-out” enrollment. _However, attention is now shifting to administrative changes rather than statutory ones._ TFVC has identified a concerning revision to newborn ImmTrac registration forms. Earlier versions clearly included **both a “GRANT CONSENT” and a “DENY CONSENT” option** , ensuring parents were explicitly informed of their right to decline participation. Since a 2022 update, the newborn form includes only a consent signature line, with the **explicit “deny consent” option removed**. Texas statute has not changed, but concerns remain about whether the administrative change on the current forms clearly reflects voluntary, affirmative consent, _especially for postpartum parents_. Click to read [the full article](https://xdzgmz.clicks.mlsend.com/tj/cl/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEyMDEyNjAsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzAyNDU2MDY1ODUyNzM1LFwiclwiOjE5MTcwMjQ5NjYyMzcyNDE2M30iLCJzIjoiZDU0OGJjZTcyNWE0MTc0ZiJ9) to compare the forms and learn why TFVC is **raising concerns about this risk to your medical privacy** :

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Taking the risk
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q22026.A9rDp6&refcode=em260630-1-b&t=1&akid=11595%2E3935704%2Ez6mYsE)
---
Friends, it’s Gabby Giffords.
When Mark and I were deciding whether to start an organization focused on gun violence prevention, we knew the challenges we would face.
Many people in Washington D.C. called it political poison to stand up against the gun lobby. The NRA had millions of dollars at their disposal, and they would use every cent to drown us out. It wasn’t going to be easy.
But after the tragic shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School, which stole 20 innocent children’s lives and six staff members, we knew that doing nothing wasn’t an option.
**So we took the risk.**
We founded what is now known as GIFFORDS — and after more than a decade of hard work, we’ve made gun safety a winning issue. We’ve passed hundreds of gun safety laws across the nation and the NRA is in the weakest position it’s ever been.
I am so grateful every single day to do this work. I have never forgotten the fights we’ve taken on and won together. The amount of lives we’ve saved — this is all because of grassroots supporters like you.
Now, we face an inflection point. As I write this, President Trump’s administration is working to roll back our progress on gun safety. They are putting all of their weight towards flooding our streets with more guns, including their latest scheme to pressure the U.S. Postal Service into freely delivering handguns through the mail.
I know that we have what it takes to end the gun violence epidemic in our country. But I cannot take on this fight alone.
**[Can you please make a donation to support GIFFORDS PAC before our end-of-quarter deadline? June is a make-or-break month for our team, and we cannot afford to fall short of our goals.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q22026.A9rDp6&refcode=em260630-1-b&t=2&akid=11595%2E3935704%2Ez6mYsE)

Peter Thiel named his surveillance company Palantir after the seeing-stones in The Lord of the Rings. His Founders Fund was an early backer of Anduril, named for Anduril, the sword reforged, the Flame of the West. The men building the digital nervous system of the American war machine reached into the same book for their branding, again and again, until Tolkien's legendarium became a kind of private dialect for Silicon Valley power.
Here is the thing about the palantiri. In the story, they are not heroic. They are the instruments that corrupt Saruman and break Denethor, the cursed stones that bind whoever looks into them to the will of Sauron. They promise omniscient vision, and they deliver enslavement. Thiel named his omniscient-vision company after the cursed object that destroys the wise men who trust it, and either he didn't notice or he didn't care, and I genuinely cannot tell you which is worse.
Last month, the Pope read the same books. He read them the other way.
In his first encyclical,[ Magnifica Humanitas](https://substack.com/redirect/8d3c4f0c-05d1-418d-a227-38ff9ea0f328?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), signed May 15 and released May 25, Pope Leo XIV quotes The Lord of the Rings directly. Paragraph 213. Footnote 187 cites The Return of the King by chapter and page, which means a Tolkien passage now sits inside Catholic Social Teaching -- the highest form of ordinary teaching the Church produces. The Pope reached into the same legendarium the founders raided for company names, and he pulled out the opposite lesson: that evil is uprooted not by powerful men holding powerful tools but by ordinary people doing ordinary, faithful work, "uprooting the evil in the fields that we know." His own line, set down right after Gandalf's, is that the civilization of love does not arrive in one spectacular gesture but in the sum of small and steadfast acts that hold the line against dehumanization.
The founders read Tolkien as a catalog of cool names for powerful tools. The Pope read him as a warning about what power does to the people who hold it. Same books. One of them was paying attention.
## **Technology is never neutral, and I learned that the hard way**
The encyclical's central claim is the one the founders will not quote, because it indicts the entire pitch.[ In his own words](https://substack.com/redirect/49271341-32ba-4728-8070-67a4fb162174?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Leo says AI cannot be considered morally neutral -- that every technical tool embodies choices and priorities through what it measures, what it ignores, what it optimizes, and how it classifies people and situations. Ethical discernment, he writes, cannot stop at asking whether we are using a system for good or bad purposes. It has to examine how the system is designed, and what vision of the human person and society is embedded in the data and the models that guide it. Every design choice reflects a vision of humanity, meaning the people building these systems bear a particular ethical and spiritual responsibility for the vision they encode.
And here is how that responsibility gets laundered. No one is ever sold a worldview. You are sold a convenience -- a faster checkout, a smarter feed, a free tool that saves you an afternoon -- and the values ride in underneath it, encoded in design choices nobody put to a vote. The genius of the thing is that the cost stays invisible right up until the moment it isn't, and by then the system is load-bearing in your life, and the question of whether you consented to its vision of you has quietly become moot.
Leo frames the danger through the oldest story we have about it: the Tower of Babel. A civilization drunk on its own reach, flattening every difference into a single uniform tongue, mistaking the ability to translate everything -- including the mystery of a human person -- into data and performance for wisdom. That is not a description of some far-off dystopia. That is the operating model of the company I handed my Social Security number to, and it is the operating model of the seeing-stone Thiel named his company after.
And Leo is precise about the human cost of being processed that way. Deep inner suffering, he writes, inevitably arises when the human person is reduced to performance, consumption, or a statistical datum. He says young people, in particular, now live under the yoke of expectations to perform, in an exasperating competitiveness that breeds anxiety and the fear of not measuring up. That is not a theological abstraction. It is a clinical description of what it feels like to be scored, ranked, optimized, and A/B tested by systems that know your data, not your name -- and it is the cost that rides in beneath every convenience, invisible until it isn't.
## **The mentality of power**
Leo is blunter than popes usually allow themselves to be about where the power now sits. He writes that innovation used to be guided largely by the State, and that today the main drivers are private, often transnational actors with resources and reach that surpass those of many governments. Technological power, he says, has taken on an unprecedented and predominantly private character, which makes it that much harder to discern, to govern, and to direct toward the common good.
Read that with Palantir's 2025 Army deal in your head. On July 31, the[ Army handed Palantir an enterprise agreement](https://substack.com/redirect/e969c4fd-76ab-4153-baf3-4f99001bf6e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) worth up to $10 billion over ten years -- the largest in the company's history -- and folded 75 separate contracts into that single vehicle. Officials were careful to say the ceiling is a ceiling, not a commitment, and much of the work was already Palantir's. But strip away the accounting, and the shape is unmistakable: a private company, named after a cursed object, wired ever deeper into the machinery of state violence -- the targeting, the logistics, the real-time intelligence -- and accountable to its shareholders, its founder's politics, and very little else. The Pope did not name Palantir. He didn't have to. He described the exact shape of the thing and let the shape do the work.
And he framed the whole choice as a binary; the entire encyclical turns on. Not enthusiasm versus fear. Not yes to technology versus no. The real choice, Leo writes, is between progress that serves individuals and peoples, and progress that subjects them to the mentality of power. A more moral AI, he warns, "is not enough if that morality is determined by a few." Because AI tends to amplify the power of whoever already holds the resources, expertise, and access to data. The machine concentrates what was already concentrated. It hands more to the people who already had the most.
That is the part that makes this a labor document wearing the costume of a technology document.
## **A Pope named Leo, 135 years later**
Pope Leo XIV signed Magnifica Humanitas on May 15 -- the 135th anniversary, to the day, of Rerum Novarum. That is not an accident, and the man chose his papal name as a similar signal. Rerum Novarum was Leo XIII's 1891 encyclical on the rights of workers, the document that founded modern Catholic social teaching, written when the Industrial Revolution was grinding agricultural and craft workers into factory labor and the Church had to decide whether it had anything to say about it. Leo XIII said capital must serve labor, not the other way around. He said a factory could not simply do whatever it wanted to the human beings inside it and call the result progress.
Leo XIV picked the name on purpose and signed on the anniversary on purpose, because he is making the same argument about the same kind of moment. The Industrial Revolution displaced the people who worked with their hands. The AI revolution is coming for the people who work with their minds: writers, coders, analysts, designers, and educators. And the encyclical refuses the easy line that this is simply the price of progress.
Leo writes that the new ways of working are not necessarily better ones. He writes that while AI promises to lift the burden of mundane tasks, in practice, it too often forces workers to adapt to the speed and demands of the machine, rather than building the machine to support the people who work. Technology should free human beings from drudgery. It should not throw them out of work in the name of cutting costs and padding profit. And then, in paragraph 155, in the same breath, the Pope expresses his hope for a "renewal of labor organizations."
Sit with that for a second. The Pope just called for stronger unions in the age of AI. The head of the global Catholic Church looked at the most powerful technology of our lifetime and concluded that the answer lies in working people organizing. That is the most useful sentence in the document for anyone who actually cares about the dignity of work, and it is the sentence the tech press skated right past, because it cannot be turned into a product.
Here in this country, we have spent decades doing the opposite. We have right-to-work laws designed to break the bargaining power that the Pope just said we need more of. We have an economy that treats labor as the first cost to cut when a new machine arrives. The encyclical is not a Democratic talking point, and I am not going to pretend it is one. But when the Pope says capital must serve the worker and workers must be free to organize, he is making an argument that the American right has spent its entire existence fighting, and the American center has spent its recent history apologizing for.
## **He said it to their faces**
He didn't leave it on the page. On June 24, Leo[ gathered twenty-eight writers at the Vatican](https://substack.com/redirect/2a7146fb-9505-4785-ab23-73adf1a83d02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- Pulitzer winners, the Nobel laureate Jon Fosse, novelists from nearly a dozen countries -- ostensibly to mark a hundred years of the Vatican's publishing house. What he actually did was stand in front of the exact workers his encyclical said the machine is coming for, and tell them the Church still needs them. "We need your imagination, your narrative creativity, and your lively thinking," he told them. Writing, he said, is an act of truth and revelation -- it reveals who we are, what we believe and hope for, the world we strive toward.
The writers in the room heard it for what it was.[ Paul Elie put it plainly afterward](https://substack.com/redirect/2261f0d4-0ba2-4a59-b0c6-0a3c3eb4b42e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): AI is a threat to literature, the Pope addressed it head-on, and the reason the world still needs writers is that we write as a free act, not as something an algorithm generated. Colum McCann said the Holy Father had been talking about storytelling, disarming language, and how AI has already penetrated the world of storytelling.
This is the encyclical's argument made flesh. The abstract claim -- that AI must serve the worker, not replace them for profit -- was narrowed to a single trade and said to its practitioners' faces. Writing is the canary. It is among the first kinds of human work the machine can convincingly counterfeit, which makes the people who do it among the first to find out whether anyone with power will say the counterfeit isn't the same thing. The Pope said it. He said it to a room that builds nothing, sells nothing, and cannot be turned into a product.
## **The blessing they want and the one they ignore**
Here is the tell, and it's in who showed up. When the Vatican unveiled the encyclical on May 25, an AI lab sent a co-founder to stand beside the Pope on the dais --[ Anthropic](https://substack.com/redirect/31b1a393-8ab0-4b6d-95cf-319a5d1ea9ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the one that markets itself as the conscientious objector of the industry, the lab that left OpenAI over safety and never lets you forget it. And here is the part that makes it more interesting than simple cynicism: the co-founder, Chris Olah, got up and admitted the problem. He said that every frontier AI lab, his own included, "operates inside a set of incentives and constraints that can sometimes conflict with doing the right thing." Then he asked the Church to be the counterweight: "We need informed critics who will tell the labs when we are failing. We need moral voices that the incentives cannot bend."
You can call that exactly what its critics called it within the hour -- ethics-washing, pope-washing, a blessing rented for the price of a photograph -- and you would not be wrong to. But notice what even the cynical reading concedes, and what the honest one makes unavoidable: a man who builds these systems stood in the Pope's hall and said out loud that the incentives bend people, and that he needs someone the incentives can't bend. The companies courting the blessing are admitting the Pope gets a vote. Leo took the handshake and named the stakes back to him: "What a great sign of hope it is that with our differences we can listen to one another."
Thiel didn't want the blessing. He reportedly told the Vice President to ignore Pope Leo on moral questions, the ethics of AI included -- not to argue with the Church, but to tune it out entirely. That is the whole spectrum of seriousness in two gestures. One camp wants the Church's stamp badly enough to admit, on the record, that its own incentives can't be trusted. The other wants the Church switched off. And the man who wants it switched off is the one who named his company after the cursed stone, which tells you he already knows what the warning says, and would simply rather you didn't read it.
## **What the machine cannot carry**
Strip away the policy, and the encyclical comes down to one passage the founders cannot build around, no matter how much computing they buy.[ In his own words, posted from his own account](https://substack.com/redirect/49271341-32ba-4728-8070-67a4fb162174?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Leo wrote that artificial intelligences do not undergo experiences, do not possess a body, do not feel joy or pain, do not mature through relationships -- that they may imitate or even simulate, but do not understand what they produce, because they lack the affective, relational, and spiritual perspective through which human beings grow in wisdom. It can wear our face. It cannot carry our soul.
That is the whole disagreement in a sentence. The men who named their companies after the seeing-stones believe the human person is a problem of insufficient data -- that with enough access and enough compute, you can model the soul and then improve on it. The Pope, reading the same books they raided for branding, says the soul is not a modeling problem. He says humanity, in all its grandeur and all its woundedness, must never be replaced or surpassed, because what makes us human is precisely the capacity for relationship and love that no machine will ever hold.
The founders read Tolkien and saw the power of the palantir. They missed that the palantir is what destroys the men who use it. The Pope read the same passage, saw the warning, and then wrote it into the law of the Church.
That is not just a verdict on the machine. It is a verdict on every man who builds one to get richer, and on every preacher who blesses him for it.
## **TL;DR**
Peter Thiel named Palantir after the cursed seeing-stones in The Lord of the Rings -- the objects that corrupt and enslave the men who use them -- and his fund helped seed Anduril, named for the Flame of the West, then both got wired into the American surveillance and war machine. Last month, Pope Leo XIV quoted the same Lord of the Rings in his first encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, and read it the opposite way: as a warning that evil is uprooted by ordinary people doing small, faithful work, not by powerful men holding powerful tools. The encyclical argues that technology is never neutral, that it carries the values of whoever builds and funds it, that private tech power has now outgrown governments, and that the real choice is between progress that serves people and progress that subjects them to the mentality of power. Signed on the 135th anniversary of Rerum Novarum, it is a labor document in disguise: it says AI must serve workers rather than replace them for profit, and it calls for a renewal of unions in the age of the algorithm. Then, in June, the Pope gathered the writers -- the workers, the machine counterfeits first -- and told them to their faces that the Church still needs them. The machine can wear our face. It cannot carry our soul. The men building it read Tolkien as an aspiration. The Pope read it as a warning. One of them was paying attention.

Peter Thiel built an empire on Tolkien's lore. Last month the Pope used the same books to tell him he read them wrong. | | | Jun 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Thanks for reading By the Ballot! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. ? Peter Thiel named his surveillance company Palantir after the seeing-stones in The Lord of the Rings. His Founders Fund was an early backer of Anduril, named for Anduril, the sword reforged, the Flame of the West. The men building the digital nervous system of the American war machine reached into the same book for their branding, again and again, until Tolkien's legendarium became a kind of private dialect for Silicon Valley power. Here is the thing about the palantiri. In the story, they are not heroic. They are the instruments that corrupt Saruman and break Denethor, the cursed stones that bind whoever looks into them to the will of Sauron. They promise omniscient vision, and they deliver enslavement. Thiel named his omniscient-vision company after the cursed object that destroys the wise men who trust it, and either he didn't notice or he didn't care, and I genuinely cannot tell you which is worse. Last month, the Pope read the same books. He read them the other way. In his first encyclical,, signed May 15 and released May 25, Pope Leo XIV quotes The Lord of the Rings directly. Paragraph 213. Footnote 187 cites The Return of the King by chapter and page, which means a Tolkien passage now sits inside Catholic Social Teaching -- the highest form of ordinary teaching the Church produces. The Pope reached into the same legendarium the founders raided for company names, and he pulled out the opposite lesson: that evil is uprooted not by powerful men holding powerful tools but by ordinary people doing ordinary, faithful work, "uprooting the evil in the fields that we know." His own line, set down right after Gandalf's, is that the civilization of love does not arrive in one spectacular gesture but in the sum of small and steadfast acts that hold the line against dehumanization. The founders read Tolkien as a catalog of cool names for powerful tools. The Pope read him as a warning about what power does to the people who hold it. Same books. One of them was paying attention. Technology is never neutral, and I learned that the hard way The encyclical's central claim is the one the founders will not quote, because it indicts the entire pitch., Leo says AI cannot be considered morally neutral -- that every technical tool embodies choices and priorities through what it measures, what it ignores, what it optimizes, and how it classifies people and situations. Ethical discernment, he writes, cannot stop at asking whether we are using a system for good or bad purposes. It has to examine how the system is designed, and what vision of the human person and society is embedded in the data and the models that guide it. Every design choice reflects a vision of humanity, meaning the people building these systems bear a particular ethical and spiritual responsibility for the vision they encode. And here is how that responsibility gets laundered. No one is ever sold a worldview. You are sold a convenience -- a faster checkout, a smarter feed, a free tool that saves you an afternoon -- and the values ride in underneath it, encoded in design choices nobody put to a vote. The genius of the thing is that the cost stays invisible right up until the moment it isn't, and by then the system is load-bearing in your life, and the question of whether you consented to its vision of you has quietly become moot. Leo frames the danger through the oldest story we have about it: the Tower of Babel. A civilization drunk on its own reach, flattening every difference into a single uniform tongue, mistaking the ability to translate everything -- including the mystery of a human person -- into data and performance for wisdom. That is not a description of some far-off dystopia. That is the operating model of the company I handed my Social Security number to, and it is the operating model of the seeing-stone Thiel named his company after. And Leo is precise about the human cost of being processed that way. Deep inner suffering, he writes, inevitably arises when the human person is reduced to performance, consumption, or a statistical datum. He says young people, in particular, now live under the yoke of expectations to perform, in an exasperating competitiveness that breeds anxiety and the fear of not measuring up. That is not a theological abstraction. It is a clinical description of what it feels like to be scored, ranked, optimized, and A/B tested by systems that know your data, not your name -- and it is the cost that rides in beneath every convenience, invisible until it isn't. The mentality of power Leo is blunter than popes usually allow themselves to be about where the power now sits. He writes that innovation used to be guided largely by the State, and that today the main drivers are private, often transnational actors with resources and reach that surpass those of many governments. Technological power, he says, has taken on an unprecedented and predominantly private character, which makes it that much harder to discern, to govern, and to direct toward the common good. Read that with Palantir's 2025 Army deal in your head. On July 31, the worth up to $10 billion over ten years -- the largest in the company's history -- and folded 75 separate contracts into that single vehicle. Officials were careful to say the ceiling is a ceiling, not a commitment, and much of the work was already Palantir's. But strip away the accounting, and the shape is unmistakable: a private company, named after a cursed object, wired ever deeper into the machinery of state violence -- the targeting, the logistics, the real-time intelligence -- and accountable to its shareholders, its founder's politics, and very little else. The Pope did not name Palantir. He didn't have to. He described the exact shape of the thing and let the shape do the work. And he framed the whole choice as a binary; the entire encyclical turns on. Not enthusiasm versus fear. Not yes to technology versus no. The real choice, Leo writes, is between progress that serves individuals and peoples, and progress that subjects them to the mentality of power. A more moral AI, he warns, "is not enough if that morality is determined by a few." Because AI tends to amplify the power of whoever already holds the resources, expertise, and access to data. The machine concentrates what was already concentrated. It hands more to the people who already had the most. That is the part that makes this a labor document wearing the costume of a technology document. A Pope named Leo, 135 years later Pope Leo XIV signed Magnifica Humanitas on May 15 -- the 135th anniversary, to the day, of Rerum Novarum. That is not an accident, and the man chose his papal name as a similar signal. Rerum Novarum was Leo XIII's 1891 encyclical on the rights of workers, the document that founded modern Catholic social teaching, written when the Industrial Revolution was grinding agricultural and craft workers into factory labor and the Church had to decide whether it had anything to say about it. Leo XIII said capital must serve labor, not the other way around. He said a factory could not simply do whatever it wanted to the human beings inside it and call the result progress. Leo XIV picked the name on purpose and signed on the anniversary on purpose, because he is making the same argument about the same kind of moment. The Industrial Revolution displaced the people who worked with their hands. The AI revolution is coming for the people who work with their minds: writers, coders, analysts, designers, and educators. And the encyclical refuses the easy line that this is simply the price of progress. Leo writes that the new ways of working are not necessarily better ones. He writes that while AI promises to lift the burden of mundane tasks, in practice, it too often forces workers to adapt to the speed and demands of the machine, rather than building the machine to support the people who work. Technology should free human beings from drudgery. It should not throw them out of work in the name of cutting costs and padding profit. And then, in paragraph 155, in the same breath, the Pope expresses his hope for a "renewal of labor organizations." Sit with that for a second. The Pope just called for stronger unions in the age of AI. The head of the global Catholic Church looked at the most powerful technology of our lifetime and concluded that the answer lies in working people organizing. That is the most useful sentence in the document for anyone who actually cares about the dignity of work, and it is the sentence the tech press skated right past, because it cannot be turned into a product. Here in this country, we have spent decades doing the opposite. We have right-to-work laws designed to break the bargaining power that the Pope just said we need more of. We have an economy that treats labor as the first cost to cut when a new machine arrives. The encyclical is not a Democratic talking point, and I am not going to pretend it is one. But when the Pope says capital must serve the worker and workers must be free to organize, he is making an argument that the American right has spent its entire existence fighting, and the American center has spent its recent history apologizing for. He said it to their faces He didn't leave it on the page. On June 24, Leo -- Pulitzer winners, the Nobel laureate Jon Fosse, novelists from nearly a dozen countries -- ostensibly to mark a hundred years of the Vatican's publishing house. What he actually did was stand in front of the exact workers his encyclical said the machine is coming for, and tell them the Church still needs them. "We need your imagination, your narrative creativity, and your lively thinking," he told them. Writing, he said, is an act of truth and revelation -- it reveals who we are, what we believe and hope for, the world we strive toward. The writers in the room heard it for what it was.: AI is a threat to literature, the Pope addressed it head-on, and the reason the world still needs writers is that we write as a free act, not as something an algorithm generated. Colum McCann said the Holy Father had been talking about storytelling, disarming language, and how AI has already penetrated the world of storytelling. This is the encyclical's argument made flesh. The abstract claim -- that AI must serve the worker, not replace them for profit -- was narrowed to a single trade and said to its practitioners' faces. Writing is the canary. It is among the first kinds of human work the machine can convincingly counterfeit, which makes the people who do it among the first to find out whether anyone with power will say the counterfeit isn't the same thing. The Pope said it. He said it to a room that builds nothing, sells nothing, and cannot be turned into a product. The blessing they want and the one they ignore Here is the tell, and it's in who showed up. When the Vatican unveiled the encyclical on May 25, an AI lab sent a co-founder to stand beside the Pope on the dais --, the one that markets itself as the conscientious objector of the industry, the lab that left OpenAI over safety and never lets you forget it. And here is the part that makes it more interesting than simple cynicism: the co-founder, Chris Olah, got up and admitted the problem. He said that every frontier AI lab, his own included, "operates inside a set of incentives and constraints that can sometimes conflict with doing the right thing." Then he asked the Church to be the counterweight: "We need informed critics who will tell the labs when we are failing. We need moral voices that the incentives cannot bend." You can call that exactly what its critics called it within the hour -- ethics-washing, pope-washing, a blessing rented for the price of a photograph -- and you would not be wrong to. But notice what even the cynical reading concedes, and what the honest one makes unavoidable: a man who builds these systems stood in the Pope's hall and said out loud that the incentives bend people, and that he needs someone the incentives can't bend. The companies courting the blessing are admitting the Pope gets a vote. Leo took the handshake and named the stakes back to him: "What a great sign of hope it is that with our differences we can listen to one another." Thiel didn't want the blessing. He reportedly told the Vice President to ignore Pope Leo on moral questions, the ethics of AI included -- not to argue with the Church, but to tune it out entirely. That is the whole spectrum of seriousness in two gestures. One camp wants the Church's stamp badly enough to admit, on the record, that its own incentives can't be trusted. The other wants the Church switched off. And the man who wants it switched off is the one who named his company after the cursed stone, which tells you he already knows what the warning says, and would simply rather you didn't read it. What the machine cannot carry Strip away the policy, and the encyclical comes down to one passage the founders cannot build around, no matter how much computing they buy., Leo wrote that artificial intelligences do not undergo experiences, do not possess a body, do not feel joy or pain, do not mature through relationships -- that they may imitate or even simulate, but do not understand what they produce, because they lack the affective, relational, and spiritual perspective through which human beings grow in wisdom. It can wear our face. It cannot carry our soul. That is the whole disagreement in a sentence. The men who named their companies after the seeing-stones believe the human person is a problem of insufficient data -- that with enough access and enough compute, you can model the soul and then improve on it. The Pope, reading the same books they raided for branding, says the soul is not a modeling problem. He says humanity, in all its grandeur and all its woundedness, must never be replaced or surpassed, because what makes us human is precisely the capacity for relationship and love that no machine will ever hold. The founders read Tolkien and saw the power of the palantir. They missed that the palantir is what destroys the men who use it. The Pope read the same passage, saw the warning, and then wrote it into the law of the Church. That is not just a verdict on the machine. It is a verdict on every man who builds one to get richer, and on every preacher who blesses him for it. TL;DR Peter Thiel named Palantir after the cursed seeing-stones in The Lord of the Rings -- the objects that corrupt and enslave the men who use them -- and his fund helped seed Anduril, named for the Flame of the West, then both got wired into the American surveillance and war machine. Last month, Pope Leo XIV quoted the same Lord of the Rings in his first encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, and read it the opposite way: as a warning that evil is uprooted by ordinary people doing small, faithful work, not by powerful men holding powerful tools. The encyclical argues that technology is never neutral, that it carries the values of whoever builds and funds it, that private tech power has now outgrown governments, and that the real choice is between progress that serves people and progress that subjects them to the mentality of power. Signed on the 135th anniversary of Rerum Novarum, it is a labor document in disguise: it says AI must serve workers rather than replace them for profit, and it calls for a renewal of unions in the age of the algorithm. Then, in June, the Pope gathered the writers -- the workers, the machine counterfeits first -- and told them to their faces that the Church still needs them. The machine can wear our face. It cannot carry our soul. The men building it read Tolkien as an aspiration. The Pope read it as a warning. One of them was paying attention. Thanks for reading By the Ballot! # Just The Truth
Your No-BS Newsletter Dear Readers, ``` Today's sponsor, the International Mission Board, is sharing how this summer's World Cup presents a rare opportunity to bring the Gospel to people from nations where openly hearing about Jesus is often impossible. Thank you for your consideration of our sponsors.
The Just The Truth Team
* * *
[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/kr5%2FxaHYbDLISamtUtyvj3cxMzVb788rn6dlANU6%2F0duBif9%2Fam7dkKEe6f5%0A3nAyDTx5rW1s7CLLgk%2F4ZamJFUg3djMbUGpMUjyOA85eWM%2BHVn0DBB6%2BVSrv%0AQuouoL9isdfKIO5Ulw3PuE7hH6bZYLMDwM9DD%2BYdb7mGz%2FojIS9nkfdp%2B88a%0Az9qeh358GCWzHY94g%2BTB3AU3DnWVxpuRqg%3D%3D%0A/386abfd0a999b89f)Dear Friend,Imagine growing up in a country where owning a Bible is illegal.Where the name of Jesus is not spoken in public. Where choosing to follow Christ could cost you your family, your job, or your freedom. Where a missionary can’t get a visa.For millions of people, this is not a hypothetical. It is everyday life.This summer, many of them are coming to the World Cup.They are coming to cheer for their national team and experience something larger than themselves. When they arrive in cities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, they will step into something they never experienced before — a place where someone can walk up to them, hand them a Gospel of John in their language, and tell them about Jesus without anyone stopping it._This moment is what we are preparing for._ IMB teams will be on the ground in Fan Zones and near stadiums throughout the tournament. Trained volunteers will be ready to have conversations, distribute resources, and connect fans with digital discipleship tools in their language that they can take home — back to countries where that kind of follow-up would otherwise be impossible.For some of these fans, this will be the only time in their lives they are handed the gospel freely.We cannot show up unprepared.You can help us be ready by giving a gift today.Here is what your gift does:
* $25 — 200 evangelism tracts placed directly into the hands of fans
* $50 — 25 soccer patches for sparking evangelistic conversations
* $100 — 100 Gospel of John booklets
* $250 — Rents an English Club outreach location where fans can hear the gospel in a welcoming space

At the Paris Olympics and the Winter Olympics, this approach worked. Thousands of spiritual conversations occurred. Tens of thousands of New Testaments were distributed. People made commitments to Christ during conversations with our teams. People interested in the gospel connected with discipleship tools that followed them home to their own countries.The World Cup is far-reaching. The opportunity to connect with people who have never had access to hear the gospel is greater than anything we have seen at a single event.But only if we are there, fully funded and fully prepared.**Will you give today to ensure our teams are on the ground and ready for the World Cup?**[Click here to give.](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/UJQwOwWxIIrWC1Gp8MmvucbpTArQ8st6wK9%2FupchNSldqpWADhHjqlPt%2FIzL%0A1cva9N3ayx7px%2F1g3vdL30SG5OV0Xbjzr8Fet9pgRndouFjY2IFe16C%2Bbsg5%0ArkTk9JZQoQuI7CNhE5tYMkA8smTyIfGHFUtMIXTbgqHO%2B7TSUe4vANMLj7d1%0A69Um%2B6Bc5k6yMhlS62U8hf1rKf5Rt3jSdg%3D%3D%0A/6b4641dac5403380) Grateful for you,

Angie Shepherd
Journeyman Alumni
Prayer and Missions Advocate International Mission Board | 3806 Monument Ave.
Richmond, VA 23230 | (804) 353-0515 ```

Good morning. Tonight is deadline night, and tomorrow my Team will begin to prepare our next public FEC fundraising report. When these numbers are released, it’s important that we’re able to show that we have the resources to run a competitive campaign. MI-07 is going to be one of the most expensive battleground districts in the country and our opponent, Tom Barrett, has a big leg up over us in terms of money. But forget about that for a moment. I want to talk about why I’m in this race to begin with. As somebody who watched Baghdad’s roads and Kabul’s roads get fixed while I was overseas, I want to see Michigan's roads get fixed. If politicians claim we don't have money to spend on health care and education in America, why are we spending billions of dollars dropping bombs on the other side of the world? There’s nothing more patriotic than loving your country so much that you want to pitch in and do your part to make it even better. I’m proud to be an American, and I’m proud to fight for the best America we can be. **So I made the decision to run for Congress.** My opponent, Tom Barrett, has become just another politician in Congress. He does whatever his GOP bosses tell him to do. Our campaign has a clear path to beating him and flipping this seat. But it’s going to be a tough fight. He’s got the entire GOP supporting him. Donald Trump, JD Vance, RFK Jr, Mike Johnson – and several other Cabinet secretaries have all come to Michigan to help Barrett. The only way we’ll be able to go toe-to-toe with their dark money is with your support. So please. **[I’m respectfully asking you to donate $10 or even $25 before midnight tonight. The only way we’ll be able to beat Barrett and take back the House is with your help. The Atlantic: Donald Trump’s Plan to Subvert the Midterms Is Already Under Way [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=063026_1&amount=25]
Team, that headline from The Atlantic says it all.
Donald Trump already promised as part of his 2024 campaign that “we’ll have it fixed so good, you’re not gonna have to vote .” Watching his actions after he lost in 2020 -- lies, denial, rallies, all leading to January 6th -- it's not hard to imagine what he's got in mind for November.
Our states run our elections. But that doesn't mean that MAGA-aligned politicians won't follow his illegal orders to interfere. It doesn't stop him from using ICE agents to intimidate at the polls or threaten eligible voters. And it doesn't stop his Department of Justice from trying to interfere through the courts, especially when more than half of the suppressive lawsuits brought to court this year were brought by the very federal department that's supposed to protect our rights.
None of that takes into account the highly partisan efforts for mid-decade redistricting as well. It's clear that the threats to the next election aren't going to stop. That's where we come in.

Peter,
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg's for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and started working for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life's easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself - but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family.
Working at Kellogg's used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that lets you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire someday.
But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost-of-living adjustments weren't keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn't right. They were making record profits - and doing it off the backs of workers.
So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HLlKrYtVVP20JnA1UcRqBNht7ihhnj3xXgeggcoKcJWymSm2OT6V69scluVHsKUR4ZRbhiswZoFAGdRfjohIw5Hc4OtUP0sESpBeJeoJdaNuMHYS5ud9ZW7bsffI_phf0gLCuVVNgNlfOQjgEoZ7ijQ52OYvBnsIWESRBrs6Fmkw3MIWfcVPhuKiJgnEA0UqDqbiy98g4ePyEuj3WwvnFwrpYBNK-EBnW-GZSoVI_fo=&c=MO5NPKDpfvrnqyB2GEx45MuNBiAV0Dagur7gUAuUiGsak-DSKkVVpg==&ch=h5D_rqMC8QrEaVShXcLmW1DGpIzA0rDUUOmp9JyHkg-RxC700dLDVw==)

Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HLlKrYtVVP20JnA1UcRqBNht7ihhnj3xXgeggcoKcJWymSm2OT6V69scluVHsKUR4ZRbhiswZoFAGdRfjohIw5Hc4OtUP0sESpBeJeoJdaNuMHYS5ud9ZW7bsffI_phf0gLCuVVNgNlfOQjgEoZ7ijQ52OYvBnsIWESRBrs6Fmkw3MIWfcVPhuKiJgnEA0UqDqbiy98g4ePyEuj3WwvnF7QxiV4iBVUJo4DrEBVZCpo=&c=MO5NPKDpfvrnqyB2GEx45MuNBiAV0Dagur7gUAuUiGsak-DSKkVVpg==&ch=h5D_rqMC8QrEaVShXcLmW1DGpIzA0rDUUOmp9JyHkg-RxC700dLDVw==)

Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians - U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer - and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country.

Dear Friend,
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)Let me tell you about Brenda Brown. For months, she worked the sidewalks of Skid Row in Los Angeles, paying homeless men and women two or three dollars apiece to put their names on voter registration forms — names that could become real ballots, mailed to an address where those people never lived. She was certain no one would ever notice. Who pays attention to Skid Row? Who would ever stand up for a homeless man being used as a tool for fraud? We did. I put on dirty clothes, sat down on that sidewalk, and let her try to recruit me — **with a hidden camera rolling the whole time.** [****](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**[CHIP IN NOW TO FUND THE NEXT INVESTIGATION →](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** A few weeks later, the Department of Justice federally charged Brenda Brown. One felony count. Up to five years in federal prison. She has since agreed to plead guilty. And at the press conference announcing the charge, the DOJ did something they almost never do for an independent journalist: they thanked us by name. **They said our footage is what made the case.** Stop and think about what that means. A camera you helped pay for put a real criminal on the path to a federal conviction. Not an op-ed. Not a hashtag. Not a "raising awareness" campaign. A conviction. Consequences. The rarest thing in American life today — a corrupt scheme actually facing justice. **[That is what your support does. It doesn't buy outrage. It buys outcomes.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** And here is why it reaches your own life, even if you've never set foot in Los Angeles: every fraudulent registration is a real ballot that can cancel out a real vote — maybe yours. When we caught Brenda Brown, we weren't just stopping one woman. We were defending the one thing that makes you a citizen instead of a subject: **the integrity of your vote.** [****](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**[DONATE NOW AND HELP US CATCH THE NEXT ONE →](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** It wasn't free, and it wasn't safe. On Skid Row my team was surrounded. **One of my guys was punched in the face and neck**. We were pepper-sprayed. We got out, kept the footage, and published it anyway. I'll be honest with you: almost no outlet on earth would send a reporter to sit on that sidewalk. It's uncomfortable. It's dangerous. There's no advertiser who wants their logo next to it. So it simply doesn't get covered — and the Brenda Browns of the world keep working in the dark. Unless someone shows up. **We show up because you make it possible.** There are more of these schemes, in more cities, operating right now. **[The only question is whether we can afford to be there with a camera when they happen.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** **[Will you stand with us today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
In Truth,James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
P.S. ****The DOJ thanked us by name. A judge will hand down the sentence. But it started with supporters deciding this work was worth funding — and a camera on a Skid Row sidewalk. The next investigation is already underway.[**Help me get it on tape.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

clean_body: Real corruption. Real camera. A real criminal conviction. Real corruption. Real camera. A real criminal conviction. | Dear Friend, me tell you about Brenda Brown. For months, she worked the sidewalks of Skid Row in Los Angeles, paying homeless men and women two or three dollars apiece to put their names on voter registration forms — names that could become real ballots, mailed to an address where those people never lived. She was certain no one would ever notice. Who pays attention to Skid Row? Who would ever stand up for a homeless man being used as a tool for fraud? We did. I put on dirty clothes, sat down on that sidewalk, and let her try to recruit me — with a hidden camera rolling the whole time. A few weeks later, the Department of Justice federally charged Brenda Brown. One felony count. Up to five years in federal prison. She has since agreed to plead guilty. And at the press conference announcing the charge, the DOJ did something they almost never do for an independent journalist: they thanked us by name. They said our footage is what made the case. Stop and think about what that means. A camera you helped pay for put a real criminal on the path to a federal conviction. Not an op-ed. Not a hashtag. Not a "raising awareness" campaign. A conviction. Consequences. The rarest thing in American life today — a corrupt scheme actually facing justice. And here is why it reaches your own life, even if you've never set foot in Los Angeles: every fraudulent registration is a real ballot that can cancel out a real vote — maybe yours. When we caught Brenda Brown, we weren't just stopping one woman. We were defending the one thing that makes you a citizen instead of a subject: the integrity of your vote. It wasn't free, and it wasn't safe. On Skid Row my team was surrounded. One of my guys was punched in the face and neck. We were pepper-sprayed. We got out, kept the footage, and published it anyway. I'll be honest with you: almost no outlet on earth would send a reporter to sit on that sidewalk. It's uncomfortable. It's dangerous. There's no advertiser who wants their logo next to it. So it simply doesn't get covered — and the Brenda Browns of the world keep working in the dark. Unless someone shows up. We show up because you make it possible. There are more of these schemes, in more cities, operating right now. In Truth,James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. **The DOJ thanked us by name. A judge will hand down the sentence. But it started with supporters deciding this work was worth funding — and a camera on a Skid Row sidewalk. The next investigation is already underway.

Peter,
Yesterday was a devastating blow for our movement. Our ballot referenda, which would empower Colorado to fight back against the Republicans' national gerrymandering campaign, were killed by Colorado's Supreme Court.
And it gets worse.
Here's who we're up against. Advance Colorado is a dark money group that refuses to disclose its donors. It was co-founded by former Governor Bill Owens, with decade-long ties to Russian oligarchs. The group runs a hidden network of front organizations and "friendly" billionaire-owned media outlets, all working together to make extreme right-wing priorities look like grassroots will. They've pushed bogus "voter fraud" measures built on the same lies Trump used to try to steal the 2020 election. The same lies that Nina Peters was supposed to sit in jail for.
The hypocrisy is staggering. But how we respond is simple. We shift from offense to defense.
First, we have to ensure Colorado stays in the fight. Red states keep rigging the rules to lock in power they didn't earn. We can't let them lock Colorado out, too.
Second, we have to defeat Advance Colorado and send them packing. This is a group focused on a lot more than redistricting, and every fight they win makes the next one easier for them.
Third, we need to stand up to the courts. After decades of court packing by radical groups like the Federalist Society, we refuse to just accept that our legal system is compromised. We're not lying down.
We need your help to keep fighting. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. body:
I'm going to Congress to put a stop to that
| | | | Hi Friend,
We are hours from our Q2 FEC deadline, and I am going to be straight with you: **I need 25 donors to give $100 before midnight to hit our goal.** That number is public. Every opponent and every donor deciding where to put money in this race will see it. I am asking you to help me make it count.
_**[GIVE $100 BEFORE MIDNIGHT](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)**_
I have been talking to people across VA-10 and I keep hearing the same thing: families here are stretched. Housing costs are up. Groceries are up. And starting today, July 1st, our energy bills will be up too.

Virginia officially rejoined the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, a regional cap-and-trade program that Dominion Energy says will result in an increase to residential electric bills. Governor Spanberger signed the legislation to bring Virginia back into RGGI, which is only going to add costs to families who are already struggling.

This is not a climate strategy, and it's certainly not how we make Virginia affordable. It is simply a burden. _And it did not have to be this way._
**The real answer to affordable, reliable, clean energy is not a cap-and-trade program that raises rates. It is an all-of-the-above energy strategy.** One that includes a long-overdue revival of clean nuclear energy.

The ADVANCE Act passed Congress in 2024 to modernize nuclear licensing. **When I go to Washington I'll push hard to build on it, cut the red tape that has stalled new reactor development for decades, and make sure Virginia families have access to energy that is both clean and affordable.**
That is the agenda. But I need to get there first.
If 25 people give $100 before midnight, we are that much closer.
_**[HELP ME REACH THIS GOAL](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)**_
If you have already given recently, a share or a forward to one person who has not yet heard about this campaign means just as much.
Thank you for being in this fight with me.
---
| | | God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Safe. Strong. Responsible._

_P.S. — Virginia was the only southern state in RGGI before Governor Youngkin withdrew in 2023. Spanberger has now brought it back. The question is whether Northern Virginia families can afford to keep absorbing costs while Washington debates energy policy. I do not think they can and I intend to do something about it._

She said “President Trump is the best President this country has ever had”.
| | | | | [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bdK7MSj8mEArGcSduJRIwsWVzp8IwNyRnIflLqc4wRYN-64ekuowhBBLtqQLlavdtRPv8hGweEkdudyDmWinUDwaOPXCb_jJcW08hO3s4MM6uqyHDodbGEctBshI-OGFBDtGBkFvxP4APvVZiU2tyQ5opfCSXH6OXOdw6Q84SR8O1xv4TQGqxe0R6A2yVIrvKc8LFTBergOjH-H_mSSmtxU-426wcw94&c=_GOZovtZ6xPLomszg-RC0nT_w6N64lfCCsOX0CB_wVAZiZT0C9CK9w==&ch=m0tbvQBWyG2IXIhRlL6eAw2MYpDTwwdP2fpqatjSWGhX7lR-qavN4Q==)

Peter,
Let me tell you all you need to know about Julia Letlow, who is now officially our opponent, in the race for Louisiana's open US Senate seat.
The Trump machine handpicked her. Trump came out swinging for her to primary Bill Cassidy after he voted to impeach him in his first term.
She proudly boasts that "President Trump is the best President this country has ever had." Polls show that about 70% of the country would beg to disagree.
---
| [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001bdK7MSj8mEArGcSduJRIwsWVzp8IwNyRnIflLqc4wRYN-64ekuowhBBLtqQLlavdtRPv8hGweEkdudyDmWinUDwaOPXCb_jJcW08hO3s4MM6uqyHDodbGEctBshI-OGFBDtGBkFvxP4APvVZiU2tyQ5opfCSXH6OXOdw6Q84SR8O1xv4TQGqxe0R6A2yVIrvKc8LFTBergPOXNtI-6HYKS3k0WBqA_6G&c=_GOZovtZ6xPLomszg-RC0nT_w6N64lfCCsOX0CB_wVAZiZT0C9CK9w==&ch=m0tbvQBWyG2IXIhRlL6eAw2MYpDTwwdP2fpqatjSWGhX7lR-qavN4Q==)
---
She is unbothered by how many times his name is in the Epstein files. She is totally fine with the billion-dollar-a-day war that could have been avoided with diplomacy.
Nothing will make her turn her back on Trump.
Letlow has a history of voting against women's rights and autonomy. At her win party, she proudly stood alongside Louisiana's Attorney General, who has spent her whole career criminalizing women's rights, going after doctors, and trying to ban the abortion pill nationwide.
If she takes office, she will help oversee the killing blow to American Democracy that is all but assured if Republicans retain control over both chambers for the remainder of Trump's 2nd term.
My name is Jamie Davis, as the Democratic Nominee for US Senate in Louisiana I am the all that stands in the way of Letlow's dark vision for our state and nation.
I am a third-generation row crop farmer farming the same Delta soil that my grandfather worked as a sharecropper. The difference is that this time around my family and I own the land and the fruits of our labor. Last night we sent the resounding message that we are not going back.
MAGA is opening the gates of hell to stop me but I am not scared. I know that we are on the right side of history.

body:
I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.

| [](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDYzMF9USy1GNC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NDIzODQtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA2MzBfVEstRjQuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTQyMzg0LTI4OTkifQ/KqmCFQC4nldJYCkzxDahNw)
---
Peter,
Do you believe in the power of prayer?
My name’s Troy Downing. When America faced its darkest hour after 9/11, I knew I couldn't just sit on the sidelines. I enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and served eight years in a Combat Search and Rescue squadron, deploying twice to Afghanistan.
On those missions, flying into danger to rescue wounded soldiers, you rely on something much bigger than yourself. Through every deployment and dark night, God’s guiding hand was our shield and protection.

| Peter,
In the lead up to TODAY'S election, Colorado is facing a stifling heatwave worsened by wildfire smoke -- and under the 90+ degree sun, one of our volunteers collapsed from heat exhaustion.
Over the last 3 days, dozens of volunteers and paid Colorado Turnout Project staff canvassed throughout CO's 8th congressional district in the scorching heat. Our objective is defeating MAGA Rep. Gabe Evans.
We handed out water bottles and set up cooling locations, but unfortunately it wasn't enough.
Thankfully, we were able to get the volunteer who collapsed the care she needed. And the rest of our intrepid volunteers carried on, continuing to battle the heat to get the job done.
They understand this election is too important to sit it out in the AC.

Like every campaign in the country, we'll publicly report how much we've raised and how many people have stepped up to support our effort. Political observers, reporters, party leaders, and our opponents will all see the same numbers, and those numbers help shape how seriously a campaign is taken. But for me, this campaign has never really been about the numbers. It's about the people I've met throughout Southwestern Pennsylvania over the past several months. _**It's about the retirees**_ who worry whether Social Security and Medicare will be there when they need them. **_It's about working families_** who feel like they are paying more for everything while Washington seems increasingly disconnected from their daily lives. **_It's about young people_** who want to build a future here but wonder whether the opportunities will exist for them to stay. Those conversations are why I decided to run for Congress. After serving eight years in the Army and twenty years as an FBI Special Agent, I never expected to enter politics. Public service has always been important to me, but I believed my service would end when I retired from government. The more I listened, however, the more convinced I became that Southwestern Pennsylvania deserves a representative who understands service, accountability, and the responsibility that comes with earning the public's trust. That's what this campaign is about. We're building a grassroots effort across all six counties of PA-14, powered not by corporate PACs or special interests, but by people who believe our communities deserve a stronger voice in Washington. **As this reporting period comes to an end, I'm asking for your help.** [If you're able, would you consider making a contribution before midnight tonight? clean_body: I never expected to enter politics | Friends, As we end the month of June, our campaign is preparing to file its next fundraising report with the Federal Election Commission. Like every campaign in the country, we'll publicly report how much we've raised and how many people have stepped up to support our effort. Political observers, reporters, party leaders, and our opponents will all see the same numbers, and those numbers help shape how seriously a campaign is taken. But for me, this campaign has never really been about the numbers. It's about the people I've met throughout Southwestern Pennsylvania over the past several months. It's about the retirees who worry whether Social Security and Medicare will be there when they need them. It's about working families who feel like they are paying more for everything while Washington seems increasingly disconnected from their daily lives. It's about young people who want to build a future here but wonder whether the opportunities will exist for them to stay. Those conversations are why I decided to run for Congress. After serving eight years in the Army and twenty years as an FBI Special Agent, I never expected to enter politics. Public service has always been important to me, but I believed my service would end when I retired from government. The more I listened, however, the more convinced I became that Southwestern Pennsylvania deserves a representative who understands service, accountability, and the responsibility that comes with earning the public's trust. That's what this campaign is about. We're building a grassroots effort across all six counties of PA-14, powered not by corporate PACs or special interests, but by people who believe our communities deserve a stronger voice in Washington. As this reporting period comes to an end, I'm asking for your help. I know there are many worthy causes asking for your support, and I don't take your generosity for granted. Whether you are able to contribute financially, volunteer your time, or simply share our message with others, I am grateful to have you with us. Thank you for believing in this campaign and for believing that public service can still make a difference. Sincerely, Alan Bradstock Candidate for Congress Army Veteran | Retired FBI Agent If you've saved your payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately. MAGA loyalist Guy Reschenthaler has consistently put party loyalty and corporate interests ahead of working families in our district. It’s time for real leadership that puts people first. Democrat Alan Bradstock is stepping up to fight for affordable healthcare, reproductive freedom, workers’ rights, and a stronger democracy, but he can’t do it without your support. * **Portnoy criticized the Democratic Party 's embrace of far-left figures,** arguing the establishment had let radical voices like Mamdani's take over. He pointed to three Mamdani-backed congressional candidates who recently unseated establishment Democrats in primary wins as evidence of the party's leftward shift.
* **Despite his interest, Portnoy expressed uncertainty about his actual electoral chances,** acknowledging he doesn't fully understand New York City's demographics or whether he could secure enough votes, though he believes he has meaningful support and credits his "real world" work experience as a contrast to career politicians.

# **SCOTUS upholds state bans on trans athletes in women 's sports**
The Supreme Court **[ruled Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/04858b24-d8ad-4f05-8971-8f064862ff84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in favor of West Virginia and Idaho in two closely watched cases, upholding state laws requiring athletes to compete on teams matching their biological sex rather than gender identity. The decisions in West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox validate similar laws already passed in 27 other states, giving more than half the country legal cover to enforce such restrictions.
* **State attorneys general celebrated the rulings as major wins for fairness in women 's athletics,** with West Virginia's John McCuskey calling it a "monumental victory" and Idaho's Raul Labrador praising the decision as protecting "decades of hard-fought progress" for female athletes.
* **Oral arguments earlier this year exposed inconsistencies in the plaintiffs ' legal strategies,** including an ACLU attorney's reluctance to define "sex" and conflicting statements about a transgender athlete's graduation timeline. Twenty-three states, including California and New York, still lack laws restricting transgender athletes from women's sports.

# **California HOA threatens homeowners with fines for flying American flags**
Residents in a San Marcos, California townhome community are refusing to comply with **[HOA orders to remove American flags from their properties,](https://substack.com/redirect/15f81e1b-7f9f-475a-965d-cc070c887535?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** despite violation notices threatening enforcement action. Homeowners Amy and Christopher Cooke received notice in May that their flag, displayed for over 20 years in honor of her husband's grandfather killed in WWII, violated common-area rules. Neighbor Terri Collins received a similar notice and plans to join the fight.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/15f81e1b-7f9f-475a-965d-cc070c887535?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The Cookes argue the HOA hasn 't justified treating their garage door frame as a common area** and have spent nearly two years researching applicable law while requesting board records. They've launched a fundraiser for potential legal costs, with leftover funds earmarked for Gold Star family causes. Legal advocates argue California law clearly prohibits HOAs from banning American flag displays outright.
* **The dispute has drawn political attention,** with gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton publicly blasting the HOA and urging residents to display more flags in defiance, timed against the backdrop of America's upcoming 250th anniversary celebrations.

* * *
# **Texas Supreme Court revives detransitioner 's medical malpractice case**
The Texas Supreme Court unanimously **[ruled to allow](https://substack.com/redirect/d7422455-4686-48c3-93cd-706a4633fec5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Soren Aldaco's malpractice lawsuit against her former therapist and Three Oaks Counseling to proceed, rejecting arguments that the statute of limitations had expired. Aldaco alleges medical interventions led to permanent disfigurement and psychological harm, and is seeking over $1 million in damages.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d7422455-4686-48c3-93cd-706a4633fec5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The ruling establishes that statute of limitations clocks can run differently in cases involving minors** guided toward irreversible gender-transition treatments, potentially opening the door for similar lawsuits nationwide. Advocacy group Independent Women's Forum called it a watershed precedent that could pressure medical providers across the country to reassess their accountability.
* **Aldaco began identifying as transgender around age 11, started hormone therapy at 17, and underwent a double mastectomy at 19** -- followed by a traumatic emergency room experience when complications arose. She has since detransitioned and become a vocal critic of gender-affirming care practices, following a similar high-profile $2 million verdict won by another detransitioner in New York earlier this year.

It's clear what they want to do -- incite someone to hurt me or my family.
I'm Christian Urrutia, the Democrat running for Congress in NH-01, America's most vulnerable open blue seat. I'm an economic populist and a first-generation Mexican-American son of immigrants. An Army officer. And someone who still believes in this country enough to fight for it.
To the far-right someone like me attaining elected office is an existential threat.
These type of extremists showed up to an event I spoke at waving Nazi flags trying to stop me from speaking (I gave my speech anyways). They send me messages telling me that my life may "abruptly come to an end." They send me pictures of nooses.
Because they hate me, they hate us, and they hate our vision.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/7334?t=1001&akid=1685%2E181023%2ElZ5gsX ][IMG]

We’re approaching an important fundraising
deadline tonight. I know we’re probably not the only campaign sending you
updates, and you probably receive a lot of requests to give, and well,
I’ll be honest: [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/7334?t=1002&akid=1685%2E181023%2ElZ5gsX ]if you’re able to give, I hope
you’ll make your first
contribution today to help us keep Michigan blue.

I wanted to send a different kind of email today to take a step back and
tell you a little bit more about why I decided to run for governor of
Michigan.

My decision to run — and most choices I’ve made in my life — all stem from
one belief: I believe everyone deserves a fair shot in life.

Growing up in a middle class family as the daughter of two special
education teachers, the values of hard work, opportunity, and serving
others were instilled in me at an early age.

I always knew I wanted to fight for justice and make a difference.

It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil
rights. Then I served as a law clerk to a federal civil rights judge in
Detroit, protecting and defending people’s civil rights and freedoms.
Then, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to make sure
all students could afford their education by freezing tuition and
expanding scholarships.

It’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life easier
for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter access.

But our work is far from finished. I’m running for governor
to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone — from our kids to our
seniors — can live and thrive.

But Michigan is one of the most competitive states in the country, and the
latest polls show this race is going to be extremely close. Winning here
won’t be easy... or cheap.

I’m committed to building a campaign built by the people, for the people.
While my Republican counterpart has already accepted $5 million from the
DeVos family funneled into a shady super PAC, [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/7334?t=1003&akid=1685%2E181023%2ElZ5gsX ]our campaign is building
real momentum, and we can’t let it stall. So please, if you can: will
you make your very
first contribution today to help us meet our
end-of-quarter fundraising deadline tonight?

Derek Schmidt

### June 30, 2026 Newsletter
---
| | Exclusive Conversation with Second Lady Usha Vance
---
| |
---
| | As our nation celebrates America's 250th birthday, we're honored to bring you a special conversation with the Second Lady of the United States, Usha Vance. In this exclusive interview, Debbie Kraulidis sits down with the Second Lady for a heartfelt discussion about the values that strengthen our families and our country. Together, they reflect on the significance of America's 250th anniversary, the joys and challenges of motherhood, her passion for promoting literacy, and the unique opportunity to serve our nation as Second Lady. Mrs. Vance offers thoughtful insights into balancing family life with public service while sharing her vision for the year ahead. Her warmth, wisdom, and commitment to America's future make this an encouraging conversation for moms, families, and anyone who believes strong homes build a strong nation. Whether you're celebrating America's milestone birthday, looking for encouragement in your own parenting journey, or simply want to hear from one of our nation's leading voices, you won't want to miss this inspiring interview. Watch the full conversation now and be inspired by this exclusive interview with Second Lady Usha Vance. [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=aTu50qqzRhr9ha0hP3qKGQi3Ftu-vXkz-4J8zX9CWB8.), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=KZxX89H1YjprNHNWcA_ZWPtEZEUhSNt0vMYfvI-hkeo.), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=cbRKa_1JCCoXfwnNuAqvptyVLPXCnTyYSpTjHEXW02Q.), or [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=Gii3s5YfjwRb8QISlIJ8QlKPJfP99h6QCXXMV-791Eo.).
