## Freedom 250: A Year Long Celebration of Our Nation
---
| |
---
| | America's 250th birthday is here, and the celebration is unlike anything our nation has ever seen! From the Great American State Fair on the National Mall to patriotic events taking place across the country all year long, Freedom 250 is inviting families to celebrate our nation's history, heritage, and the blessings of liberty together. Some of the exciting events include:
* The Great American State Fair featuring all 50 states, concerts, exhibits, family activities, and the Faith & Family Pavilion, where Moms for America is welcoming visitors.
* The Freedom Trucks are interactive traveling museums that bring America's story to communities nationwide.
* Spectacular celebrations at Mount Rushmore, a historic International Naval Review in New York Harbor, and record-breaking Independence Day fireworks.
* The Patriot Games, Freedom 250 Grand Prix, student art exhibitions, and countless opportunities for families to learn and celebrate together.

The [Freedom 250](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=qs1D0kcP8R4Nbi00-kEgycTGUz5WVzIVYRbQ3eJLBmc.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9tMjUwLm9yZy8iLCJyIjoiMzI5Y2RiNGEtZWU2Yi00MzFmLTliZmUtOGJiODEwZDQ1ZGUyIiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiYjM4MzhiZjgtZmFiMC00MWI5LTk2NzMtZThjNmJlZmI2NTc3In0) website also offers outstanding family resources, including history videos from Hillsdale College, printable Founders Museum activities, and educational tools that make learning about America's founding both fun and meaningful. This historic anniversary reminds us that freedom is worth celebrating and preserving for future generations. We hope you'll take part in the festivities happening in your community and make this anniversary one your family will never forget. Read the [full blog](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=XdTA4Ql32L8IRRKwbyVgoakqMuDctHmGvQOGZLVJC5A.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvYmxvZyIsInIiOiIzMjljZGI0YS1lZTZiLTQzMWYtOWJmZS04YmI4MTBkNDVkZTIiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) for event details, family resources, and ways your family can join the celebration throughout the year. As moms, we have the privilege of passing America's story to the next generation. Let's spend this entire year celebrating the greatness of America and the freedoms that make our nation exceptional.
---
| | | |
---
| |
## Join the 1776 Club
---
| | [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/b2PyO_P4l/c?w=uOMvw7bomalNhBG95os8CD1T3_6_M6NRW1n09stYCrw.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9tb21zZm9yYW1lcmljYS5zdG9yZS8iLCJyIjoiMWFkMDVkZGQtZTAzOC00YzBiLThiNDgtODU3OWRiZDdlMTc3IiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiYjM4MzhiZjgtZmFiMC00MWI5LTk2NzMtZThjNmJlZmI2NTc3In0)
---
| | On this very special Fourth of July, we're launching something we've been building just for you. It's called the 1776 Club, and we're inviting 250 Founding Members to join us by the close of Fourth of July weekend. Two hundred and fifty years ago, ordinary men and women made extraordinary sacrifices so that future generations could live in freedom. Today, that story continues with us.As moms, we know the future isn't built only in the halls of government. It's built around our kitchen tables, in bedtime stories, in family traditions, and in the values we pass from one generation to the next. That's exactly what the 1776 Club is about. It's a place for moms who believe that faith, freedom, and family aren't just words, they're a way of life worth protecting, worth funding, and worth passing on. Watch your inbox on July 4th. A very special invitation is coming your way. We hope you'll be one of our 250 Founding Members who help lay the foundation for the next generation of families who will change the world.
---
| | | |
---
| |
---
| In Truth & Liberty, Kimberly Fletcher

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Before tonight’s deadline, I want to share a lesson I learned about faith.
body:
I’m asking you to have faith that we can finally unseat corrupt Governor Greg Abbott and flip Texas together.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In just a minute, I’m going to personally ask you to [**make a $5 donation to my campaign for governor before tonight’s midnight deadline.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260630_1_leap.XpAxd6&refcode=em20260630-1461&amount=5&t=1&akid=1461%2E299639%2E1sD1Jp)
Before I do, I hope you’ll let me share **an important lesson I’ve learned about faith.**
Back in 2021, the Texas GOP was ramming an extreme anti-voter bill through the State House. The voter suppression bill they were pushing was ugly. It was dangerous. And I knew that staying put would mean letting Texans lose their freedom to vote.
So I took a leap of faith. I chose to walk off the floor.
But I knew I couldn’t stop this bill on my own. I needed my fellow Democratic legislators with me in order to break quorum. So I stood up, and I texted other legislators:
_“A leap of faith only works if you take it.”_
Together, we ran out the clock and stopped a bill designed to silence Texas voters. That quorum break protected Sunday morning voting — a sacred tradition in Black churches — and blocked a provision that would have allowed partisan judges to overturn election results without evidence. And we earned that victory together.
**Just like I needed my fellow Texas Democrats by my side on that day five years ago, I’m asking you to join me today.** I’m asking you to have faith that we can finally unseat corrupt Governor Greg Abbott and flip Texas together.
Each time you chip in to our people-powered campaign, you’re doing it alongside thousands of others who also believe in our power to win a brighter future for every Texan.
**[Can I count on you to donate for the very first time before tonight’s big deadline?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260630_1_leap.XpAxd6&refcode=em20260630-1461&amount=5&t=2&akid=1461%2E299639%2E1sD1Jp)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260630_1_leap.XpAxd6&amount=5&refcode=em20260630-1461&t=21&akid=1461%2E299639%2E1sD1Jp)
_A leap of faith only works if you take it. And when you do, others will leap with you._
— Gina

# Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S. negotiators arrive in Doha as Iran rules out direct meetings:**
* President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff are in Doha but will not hold direct meetings with Iranian officials, spokesperson for Qatar's Foreign Ministry Majed Al-Ansari said on Tuesday. Instead, they are expected to meet with mediators to discuss the progress of negotiations.
* Al-Ansari said the $6 billion in frozen Iranian assets has not yet been transferred to Iran, adding that the release of the funds is directly linked to the progress of negotiations between Tehran and Washington.
* Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran has no plans to meet U.S. officials "at any level in the next few days." He said discussions in Doha would instead focus on "the implementation of clauses of the memorandum of understanding, including the clause related to the release of Iran's restricted assets with the Qatari parties," adding: "We have not planned any meeting with the American side at any level for the next few days."
* **Oman backs Iran 's "service fee" framework for Strait of Hormuz transit: **Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi [backed](https://substack.com/redirect/8393816a-982a-447a-8a7e-33667760d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the legal basis for Iran's proposed Strait of Hormuz fees in an interview with Monte Carlo Doualiya on Monday, saying Oman opposes transit tolls but distinguishes those from voluntary fees for maritime, environmental, and navigational services.
* Al-Busaidi said Iran bears primary responsibility under the memorandum for clearing roughly 80 mines and securing shipping lanes, with Oman contributing through regional and international efforts, and that any future arrangements would remain within international law, a position that aligns more closely with Iran's stance than Washington's.
* **Iran rejects French offer to help clear Strait of Hormuz mines:** Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi [pushed back](https://substack.com/redirect/cd2bc2ab-8ca7-455b-818d-82b43991c410?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after French President Emmanuel Macron said France would work with partners to clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz, saying the Islamabad memorandum assigns demining exclusively to Iran and that no other country will be permitted to participate "in principle."
* Gharibabadi warned France against what he called provocations that could "further complicate" the situation, describing conditions in the Strait as "sensitive and complex."
* **Qatar suspends recreational maritime activity:** Qatar temporarily [suspended](https://substack.com/redirect/5e196c3e-00fe-44cc-80e6-febe4a60b78a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sailing and most non-commercial maritime activities until further notice on Monday, citing public safety amid heightened regional unrest, according to Al Jazeera.
* The Transport Ministry said the measure covers leisure boats, fishing vessels, jet skis, and other small craft, while vessels covered by international maritime conventions remain exempt, a day after a Qatari national was reportedly killed by shrapnel.
* **Pezeshkian: U.S. deal approved by Supreme Leader, backed by National Council:** Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/8bafa505-8db3-4abc-a569-02b16cb2ee88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his government's negotiations with the United States on Tuesday following criticism from some conservative factions, saying the talks were conducted in "full and continuous coordination" with the Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamanei, the Islamic Republic News Agency reported. Speaking in Qom, Pezeshkian said the final text of the agreement had received "strong backing" from the Supreme National Security Council, adding that the government had pursued "the rights of the Iranian people from a position of dignity, authority and safeguarding national interests" and "has not and will not succumb to the enemy's imposed demands."
* **Two IRGC members killed in shooting near Iran-Iraq border:** Two members of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/0144026e-e1ae-421e-830c-d6ab5cc174c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and two others wounded in a shooting in Paveh County near Iran's border with Iraq, Iranian state media reported on Tuesday via Anadolu Agency. According to the IRGC's Public Relations Office in Kermanshah Province, unidentified gunmen opened fire at the entrance of a house on Monday evening in what it described as a "cowardly and treacherous terrorist act." The two men killed were identified as local IRGC members. The IRGC said an investigation is underway to establish the circumstances of the attack and identify those responsible.

# Lebanon
* **Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri rejects U.S.-backed "Trilateral Framework" with Israel: **Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/6261252e-ed6f-4e79-a276-b919135be639?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the U.S.-backed "Trilateral Framework" with Israel, calling it a set of "diktats" that is "ten times worse" than the unpopular 1983 May 17 Agreement, which stipulated the withdrawal of Israeli forces following their invasion of Lebanon and siege of Beirut, Al-Akhbar reported on Monday.
* Berri said the framework's most dangerous aspect is its potential to incite internal Lebanese divisions.
* Berri also said the deal conditions Israeli withdrawal on Lebanon on meeting a list of demands, and that it makes no reciprocal demands of Israel. "This agreement will not pass, and it will not be implemented," Berri said.
* **Israeli stun grenades, airstrike target southern Lebanon in continued ceasefire violations:** Israeli forces continued operations across southern Lebanon on Tuesday, with a drone [dropping](https://substack.com/redirect/1775fa31-23d0-420e-9268-aec22b301a58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a stun grenade near the Ain Badda spring between Aita Al-Jabal and Hadatha, as farmers were tending their land, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. No injuries were reported. Israeli drones also dropped stun grenades on a house in Hadatha and on the eastern outskirts of Braachit in Bint Jbeil District, while Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/7fbaf239-51b0-4d64-ba91-5c18bc8e961d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a predawn airstrike on Deir Siryan in Marjeyoun District.
* **Israeli soldier wounded near Beaufort Castle:** An Israeli reservist was "seriously injured" Monday in an explosion in southern Lebanon near Beaufort Castle, in the Nabatieh area, the Israeli army said, according to Haaretz. The military said it was still investigating the incident and that the soldier was hospitalized.
* **About 400,000 displaced Lebanese have returned home since March, minister says:** About 400,000 forcibly displaced people in Lebanon, roughly 40% of the more than 1.2 million uprooted since Israel re-escalated its war on March 2, have [returned](https://substack.com/redirect/1de653c2-8e43-4c4e-aba5-3206dc71f18b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to their home regions, Social Affairs Minister Haneen Sayed said Monday.
* The number of people sheltering in reception centers has fallen to 13,000 from 37,000, he said, though many remain unable to return as Israel occupies a strip of southern Lebanon behind the "Yellow Line."

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded:** Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 26 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,066 killed, with 173,514 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,053 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,406, while 786 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israeli bombardment, home demolitions across Gaza:** Several Palestinians were [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/f3c7da6b-d45b-48cb-844f-c935b085b349?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday after an Israeli airstrike targeted a group of people near the Sheikh Radwan junction in Gaza City, according to WAFA. In southern Gaza, Israeli troops carried out four large-scale demolitions of homes and civilian structures in Khan Younis, while artillery shelled northwestern Rafah. In Gaza City, Israeli forces destroyed homes in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood, alongside heavy gunfire in Shujaiya.
* **Israeli strike on displaced Palestinians kills two, wounds 20:** An Israeli drone strike on displaced people in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/a4a39652-f516-4aa7-9662-83bc6d70fd18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinians and wounded more than 20 others Monday, according to medical sources cited by Al Jazeera.
* Separately, a Palestinian man was shot and killed by Israeli forces in Al-Qarara, northwest of Khan Younis, according to WAFA, bringing Monday's death toll from Israeli attacks across Gaza to at least eight, two of whom were children.
* **Israel shoots and kills 15-year-old Palestinian in West Bank:** Israeli forces [shot](https://substack.com/redirect/3a34804b-1fdb-425c-952a-bd16bdaeb6f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 15-year-old in the head and chest on Monday during a raid in el-Bireh, near Ramallah, WAFA reported.
* The head of the area's governorate called the killing a "clear-cut execution in broad daylight" and said it made a mockery of "institutions that claim to uphold democracy and human rights."
* B'Tselem, the Israeli human rights organization, issued a report on Monday saying Israeli forces have killed 241 Palestinian children and teenagers in the occupied West Bank since October 7, 2023.
* **Hamas delegation arrives in Cairo to discuss Gaza ceasefire roadmap:** A Hamas delegation arrived in Cairo on Tuesday for talks with Egyptian officials and mediators on implementing the Gaza ceasefire agreement and advancing negotiations on the next phase, according to a statement released by the group. Hamas official Taher Al-Nunu said the delegation, led by Zaher Jabarin, will press for an end to "the escalating Israeli violations" in the Gaza Strip, including "the daily killings and assassinations," while demanding that Israel allow the full entry of humanitarian supplies and reconstruction materials and implement the remaining provisions of the Sharm el-Sheikh Agreement. The delegation will also discuss the second phase of the roadmap presented by Nickolay Mladenov, leading up to "full Israeli withdrawal from all of Gaza." Read the latest on Gaza negotiations from Drop Site's Jeremy Scahill and Jawa Ahmad **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/f0e81ba1-b9b4-4268-bc3a-e45e0cfdd27b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
* **Committee to Protect Journalists set to narrow journalist definition:** The **Committee to Protect Journalists** (CPJ) will reportedly [revise](https://substack.com/redirect/0b530fec-e5ae-47d4-944e-84395f993d33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its definition of who qualifies as a journalist in a move that would broadly exclude slain Palestinian and Lebanese journalists working for government-funded outlets, while journalists from Israel, the U.S., and Ukraine at state-funded or military-embedded outlets would remain classified as journalists. The change follows pressure from the right-wing publication The Free Beacon, which has repeatedly alleged that Palestinian and Lebanese journalists were militants or cited their political views to justify their killings by Israeli forces.
* Later on Monday, Drop Site News publisher **Dr. Nika Soon-Shiong** [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/944becb7-970c-44ee-9bcd-9f15a93f8564?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that she had been removed from the CPJ board, after opposing this proposal. Soon-Shiong published an email she sent to the board arguing that the proposal would politicize CPJ's mission, could exclude journalists based on their employer or alleged conduct, and could undermine protections for journalists, particularly those in Gaza.
* An internal CPJ email shared with Drop Site calls reports that the organization plans to change its definition "false allegations" and "untrue." It says the review, led by CPJ's Middle East and North Africa team, is focused on its documentation of journalists killed in the Israel-Gaza war after some individuals previously listed as journalists were later determined to have been combatants, and is expected to be completed in July.
* **Released Palestinian detainees describe starvation, sleep deprivation at Israel 's Ofer Prison: **Released Palestinian detainees [described](https://substack.com/redirect/c603cebb-9a2e-4b6a-98f8-e5ec270b6fe8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) days of starvation, sleep deprivation, and humiliation inside Israel's Ofer Prison in interviews conducted by Mohamed Ahmed for Drop Site News.
* Nasser Ghaleb Mohammed Al-Haj Ahmad, 35, said detainees were denied food, water, sleep, and bathrooms. "If you sleep, you sleep on iron. There is no sleep, no life."
* Jamal Shukri Mohammed Abu Shanab, 68, said detainees ate only plain yogurt for 10 days and were bound, forced onto their stomachs, and jolted awake whenever they tried to sleep.
* The International Committee of the Red Cross, which has been denied access to Israeli-held Palestinian detainees since October 7, 2023, said it transferred 13 released Palestinians from the Kerem Abu Salem crossing to the hospital Monday, with more than 9,400 Palestinians, including over 3,200 held without charge, still imprisoned by Israel.
* **Israeli lawmaker says bill to bar Red Cross visits to Palestinian prisoners defeated:** Israeli lawmaker Ofer Cassif, the only Jewish member of the anti-occupation Hadash party in the Knesset, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/b7dbc709-d6a7-4ea2-bb2a-9e9499e9c6d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that lawmakers defeated a bill that would have barred the Red Cross from visiting Palestinian detainees in Israeli prisons. Cassif said the measure was intended to prevent the world from seeing "the marks of torture and inhumane conditions" on Palestinian prisoners. He called for the immediate resumption of Red Cross visits to prisons.

* **Primaries in Colorado on Tuesday:**
* Colorado's Democratic establishment is reportedly increasingly [concerned](https://substack.com/redirect/3b33f248-0762-45d4-93c6-308a5be034bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that a progressive wave could reshape Tuesday's primaries, with Politico reporting that Sen. **John Hickenlooper** is in a "dead heat" with state Sen. **Julie Gonzales** in Denver and that Rep. **Diana DeGette 's** campaign is alarmed by internal polling showing her race with progressive challenger **Melat Krios** tightening. Allies of Sen. **Michael Bennet** also reportedly acknowledged his gubernatorial race against Colorado Attorney General **Phil Weiser** is closer than expected, per private polling cited by Politico.
* A last-minute infusion of funds into DeGette's campaign from AIPAC and big tech is discussed in the latest from **Ryan Grim** , **Julian Andreone** , and **Toby Jaffe** for Drop Site, available **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/b46d3b0a-68a6-469f-9eea-4c5cc8893ca1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Monday 's Supreme Court decisions:**
* **Upholds state laws counting late-arriving mail ballots:** The Supreme Court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/d433f17c-384a-4adf-a27a-421d1428ed98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 5-4 Monday that election officials may count postmarked mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day, rejecting a Republican National Committee challenge to a Mississippi law and finding it does not conflict with federal law setting Election Day in early November. The ruling, authored by Justice Amy **Coney Barrett** with two conservatives joining the three liberals in the majority, keeps the Mississippi law and similar measures in 13 other states in effect ahead of November's midterms.
* **Splits on Trump 's power to fire independent agency officials, blocks Fed's Cook ouster but allows FTC firing: **The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 Monday that President Donald Trump [cannot](https://substack.com/redirect/b47ff957-f1b3-4be1-b6b0-0ae85b4de83d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fire Federal Reserve board member**Lisa Cook** for now, with Chief Justice **John Roberts** writing that for-cause protections shield the Fed from being treated as "at-will employment." In a separate 6-3 ruling, however, the Court overturned the 1935 precedent Humphrey's Executor v. United States and allowed Trump to remove Federal Trade Commission member**Rebecca Kelly Slaughter** without cause. Roberts wrote in the Slaughter ruling that "subordinates who exercise the president's power are subject to removal by him." Trump indicated on Truth Social that he would still seek to fire Cook, whom he has accused of committing mortgage fraud. Cook denies the claims.
* **Rejects Trump 's bid to overturn $5 million E. Jean Carroll verdict: **The Supreme Court [declined](https://substack.com/redirect/cdecc5a1-ab79-4db8-9d35-abbdab67c0c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday, without explanation or noted dissents, to hear President Donald Trump's appeal of a jury's $5 million finding that he sexually abused writer **E. Jean Carroll** at a Manhattan department store in the mid-1990s and later defamed her, according to the Associated Press.
* **AOC introduces NDAA amendment that could halt U.S. military aid to Israel:** Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez**(D-N.Y.) [introduced](https://substack.com/redirect/88286924-2a16-4b61-9e69-b2bd63719fee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act on Monday that could effectively halt offensive and defensive U.S. military aid to Israel.
* The proposal would require U.S. defense transfers to comply with international law and, building on Section 620I of the Foreign Assistance Act, would require the president to affirmatively certify that a recipient isn't restricting U.S.-backed humanitarian aid.
* Ocasio-Cortez's amendment requires the president to affirmatively certify that the laws banning the restriction of aid are being followed and also requires Congress to authorize the weapons transfers before they can proceed.
* Ocasio-Cortez has also pursued amendments that focus on the U.S. military's presence in Latin America, requiring the Pentagon to publish a report on its use of military facilities in Puerto Rico, demanding an accounting of human rights violations in Peru between 2022 and 2024 and in Colombia for the last 3 decades, and barring military cooperation with Ecuador's current government.
* The congresswoman [spoke](https://substack.com/redirect/f6aaff32-75bf-4e1b-8dc3-63de00a5a2ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Drop Site's Julian Andreone on Tuesday about her proposed amendments. **Watch[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/f6aaff32-75bf-4e1b-8dc3-63de00a5a2ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **House Rules Committee blocks Massie-Khanna amendment to remove Israel tech provision from NDAA:** The House Rules Committee [blocked](https://substack.com/redirect/6a0adcc7-4dea-468e-ad93-b96179361697?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a bipartisan amendment from Reps. **Thomas Massie** (R-Ky.) and**Ro Khanna**(D-Calif.)**** that sought to remove a provision expanding U.S.-Israel military technology integration from the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act, meaning it will not receive a House floor vote.
* The underlying provision, which remains in the NDAA, would deepen U.S.-Israel defense technology cooperation, including joint weapons development and other military collaboration.
* **Progressive Caucus chair Greg Casar to back Massie amendment cutting U.S. military aid to Israel:** Rep. **Greg Casar**(D-Texas), chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f8476403-e350-4c3f-bb7c-373c97e33dc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that he will vote for Rep. **Thomas Massie 's** amendment to end U.S. taxpayer-funded military aid for Israel, arguing the Israeli government "committed war crimes in Gaza and helped drag America into war with Iran."
* The amendment would bar funds in the bill from going to Israel and cut Foreign Military Financing by $3.3 billion, though it would not constitute an arms embargo or ban all U.S. arms sales to Israel.
* **Jewish Voice for Peace Action endorses Abdul El-Sayed for Michigan Senate seat:** Jewish Voice for Peace Action [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/e095783f-f6a8-4976-ad57-6e4660232b4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its first-ever Senate endorsement to Michigan Senate candidate **Abdul El-Sayed** on Monday, citing his consistent stance on human rights and progressive foreign policy.
* **Colorado Supreme Court blocks Democratic redistricting effort:** The Colorado Supreme Court [dealt](https://substack.com/redirect/9cb92a19-34ab-4d34-be7b-8bd930b66c5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a blow Monday to Democratic efforts to redraw the state's congressional maps ahead of 2028, ruling that twin ballot initiatives violated the state constitution's "single subject requirement" because each measure was contingent on the other's passage.
* Democrats behind the effort said time has run out to gather the roughly 125,000 signatures needed by August 3 to qualify for November's ballot, dealing a setback to a plan that aimed to draw up to three new Democratic-leaning districts as part of the broader national redistricting fight.
* **Rep. Yassamin Ansari calls Israel 's actions in Gaza "genocide," vows to reject AIPAC funding: **Rep. **Yassamin Ansari** of Arizona, the first Iranian American Democrat elected to Congress, [called](https://substack.com/redirect/2af6c0f5-c3d3-4ffc-8f81-fb43a653168d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israel's actions in Gaza and Lebanon a "genocide" and pledged to stop accepting money from pro-Israel groups including AIPAC, in an interview with Zeteo on Monday.
* The shift marks a reversal for Ansari, who won her 2024 primary as a self-described "proud pro-Israel progressive" backed by Democratic Majority for Israel, opposed Sen.**Bernie Sanders 's **effort to block $20 billion in arms sales to Israel, and voted to sanction the International Criminal Court over its warrants for Israeli leaders.
* **DOJ opens investigation into Sen. Ruben Gallego days after Senate Ethics Committee clears him:** The Justice Department has [opened](https://substack.com/redirect/55731ef6-ca9a-47b7-a68d-826c45ae2223?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an investigation into Sen. **Ruben Gallego** (D-Ariz.) stemming from a "whistleblower complaint" out of Southern California related to his use of a political committee's PAC to fund family trips to Miami, Chicago, Disneyland, and Disney World, coming days after the Senate Ethics Committee closed its inquiry into separate sexual misconduct and campaign finance allegations after finding no rule violations.
* Gallego, who has hired former Biden deputy press secretary **Andrew Bates** for crisis communications help amid fallout from his public friendship with former Rep. **Eric Swalwell** , has denied wrongdoing and said the allegations are politically motivated as he weighs a potential 2028 presidential run.
* **NYC Council Member Paladino suggests CIA, FBI should "neutralize" DSA leaders: **New York City Council Member **Vickie Paladino** [suggested](https://substack.com/redirect/25a55a9a-2d95-4df6-bfb4-6a2c6db33585?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a post on Monday that the CIA and FBI once would have "neutralized one way or another" "unabashed revolutionaries" while sharing a post identifying Democratic Socialists of America leadership members.
* Congressional candidate **Darializa Avila Chevalier** called the remarks a "thinly veiled call" for the federal government to kill DSA members and demanded Paladino's expulsion from the City Council.

# Other International News
* **Iraq sets September 30 deadline for Iran-aligned factions to disarm under U.S. pressure:** Iraq's government has [given](https://substack.com/redirect/4c56c3d7-d1d2-4254-b109-f145a385db45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran-aligned armed factions until September 30 to disarm. The deadline was announced ahead of a visit to the U.S. by Iraq's new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi. Iraqi government spokesman Haidar al-Aboudi said Monday that groups possessing weapons would face legal action after that date, which also marks the end of the international anti-ISIS coalition's presence in the country.
* Two factions, Kataeb Imam Ali and Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have already agreed to turn over administration of their brigades to the state, while others among Iraq's dozens of Iran-aligned factions, some of which attacked U.S. bases during this year's Iran war, have yet to comply, according to AFP and The New Arab.
* Also on Monday, Iraqi security forces, including the elite Counter-Terrorism Service, [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/35844fc2-c24e-4b67-988d-c4e0aebb3d9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 47 people, including lawmakers, senior officials, and prominent politicians, in an anticorruption crackdown ordered by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, raiding homes in Baghdad's Green Zone and other neighborhoods. Iraq's Federal Commission of Integrity said the arrests were based on judicial warrants tied to alleged misappropriation of public funds, with lawmakers' parliamentary immunity lifted beforehand. They follow last month's arrest of Deputy Oil Minister Adnan al-Jumaili and the seizure of roughly $86 million in cash.
* **Russian strikes across Ukraine kill at least eight, including a child:** Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/507fdd0c-c9bb-4fd8-9e4c-f78df5829e69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least eight people and wounded 34 others Monday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, including five killed and 28 wounded in a missile attack on Dnipro and three killed and six wounded, among them a child, in a drone attack on Zaporizhzhia.
* Additional Russian strikes hit the Sumy, Odesa, Chernihiv, Kherson, and Kharkiv regions.
* The Kremlin said Monday that Russia's position on a peace deal has remained unchanged since 2024, when Putin said Kyiv must withdraw from four regions Moscow claims and drop its NATO bid.
* **Rubio meets Libyan commander Saddam Haftar:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio [met](https://substack.com/redirect/70d437b3-e585-4875-901f-40a0b4c99614?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday with Libyan National Army Deputy Commander Saddam Haftar to discuss unification efforts in the country and possible cooperation between the U.S. and Haftar's LNA, according to a State Department readout.
* The meeting came the same day a new documentary by Evident, Sudan War Monitor, and LightHouse presented new evidence that Haftar has worked with the UAE to facilitate arms and training for Sudan's RSF militia.
* **South Africa deploys police as anti-immigrant groups ' deportation "deadline" sparks fear, business closures: **Businesses across South African cities [closed](https://substack.com/redirect/460a84a4-e883-499f-916a-9cf792734b2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and police were deployed on Tuesday as anti-immigrant protests continued nationwide ahead of a "deadline" anti-immigrant groups have given undocumented foreign nationals to leave, falsely claiming they will otherwise face arrest and deportation, according to Al Jazeera.
* President Cyril Ramaphosa said the right to protest "does not allow people to threaten or intimidate others, or to engage in acts of vandalism or violence."
* Weeks of xenophobic violence in the country have killed people from Mozambique, Ethiopia, and Malawi, according to AFP, with thousands of foreign nationals, including some in the country legally, sheltering at consulates or being repatriated by their home countries.
* **UK national security bill could expose journalists to "terrorism" prosecution, legal experts warn: **British journalists reporting from countries like Iran could [face](https://substack.com/redirect/98fd9a50-0f3a-4e70-a683-767bbf81a4bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) terrorism prosecutions under a UK national security bill expected to complete its final parliamentary stages this week, according to reporting Monday in the Guardian.
* Legal expert David Anderson warned the bill could criminalize foreign correspondents for obtaining information from sources within state-designated groups because it lacks explicit protections for journalists, and press freedom groups are urging amendments.

Iran and Ceasefire U.S. negotiators arrive in Doha as Iran rules out direct meetings: President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff are in Doha but will not hold direct meetings with Iranian officials, spokesperson for Qatar's Foreign Ministry Majed Al-Ansari said on Tuesday. Instead, they are expected to meet with mediators to discuss the progress of negotiations. Al-Ansari said the $6 billion in frozen Iranian assets has not yet been transferred to Iran, adding that the release of the funds is directly linked to the progress of negotiations between Tehran and Washington. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran has no plans to meet U.S. officials "at any level in the next few days." He said discussions in Doha would instead focus on "the implementation of clauses of the memorandum of understanding, including the clause related to the release of Iran's restricted assets with the Qatari parties," adding: "We have not planned any meeting with the American side at any level for the next few days." Oman backs Iran 's "service fee" framework for Strait of Hormuz transit: Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi the legal basis for Iran's proposed Strait of Hormuz fees in an interview with Monte Carlo Doualiya on Monday, saying Oman opposes transit tolls but distinguishes those from voluntary fees for maritime, environmental, and navigational services. Al-Busaidi said Iran bears primary responsibility under the memorandum for clearing roughly 80 mines and securing shipping lanes, with Oman contributing through regional and international efforts, and that any future arrangements would remain within international law, a position that aligns more closely with Iran's stance than Washington's. Iran rejects French offer to help clear Strait of Hormuz mines: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi after French President Emmanuel Macron said France would work with partners to clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz, saying the Islamabad memorandum assigns demining exclusively to Iran and that no other country will be permitted to participate "in principle." Gharibabadi warned France against what he called provocations that could "further complicate" the situation, describing conditions in the Strait as "sensitive and complex." Qatar suspends recreational maritime activity: Qatar temporarily sailing and most non-commercial maritime activities until further notice on Monday, citing public safety amid heightened regional unrest, according to Al Jazeera. The Transport Ministry said the measure covers leisure boats, fishing vessels, jet skis, and other small craft, while vessels covered by international maritime conventions remain exempt, a day after a Qatari national was reportedly killed by shrapnel. Pezeshkian: U.S. deal approved by Supreme Leader, backed by National Council: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian his government's negotiations with the United States on Tuesday following criticism from some conservative factions, saying the talks were conducted in "full and continuous coordination" with the Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamanei, the Islamic Republic News Agency reported. Speaking in Qom, Pezeshkian said the final text of the agreement had received "strong backing" from the Supreme National Security Council, adding that the government had pursued "the rights of the Iranian people from a position of dignity, authority and safeguarding national interests" and "has not and will not succumb to the enemy's imposed demands." Two IRGC members killed in shooting near Iran-Iraq border: Two members of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were and two others wounded in a shooting in Paveh County near Iran's border with Iraq, Iranian state media reported on Tuesday via Anadolu Agency. According to the IRGC's Public Relations Office in Kermanshah Province, unidentified gunmen opened fire at the entrance of a house on Monday evening in what it described as a "cowardly and treacherous terrorist act." The two men killed were identified as local IRGC members. The IRGC said an investigation is underway to establish the circumstances of the attack and identify those responsible. Lebanon Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri rejects U.S.-backed "Trilateral Framework" with Israel: Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri the U.S.-backed "Trilateral Framework" with Israel, calling it a set of "diktats" that is "ten times worse" than the unpopular 1983 May 17 Agreement, which stipulated the withdrawal of Israeli forces following their invasion of Lebanon and siege of Beirut, Al-Akhbar reported on Monday. Berri said the framework's most dangerous aspect is its potential to incite internal Lebanese divisions. Berri also said the deal conditions Israeli withdrawal on Lebanon on meeting a list of demands, and that it makes no reciprocal demands of Israel. "This agreement will not pass, and it will not be implemented," Berri said. Israeli stun grenades, airstrike target southern Lebanon in continued ceasefire violations: Israeli forces continued operations across southern Lebanon on Tuesday, with a drone a stun grenade near the Ain Badda spring between Aita Al-Jabal and Hadatha, as farmers were tending their land, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. No injuries were reported. Israeli drones also dropped stun grenades on a house in Hadatha and on the eastern outskirts of Braachit in Bint Jbeil District, while Israeli warplanes a predawn airstrike on Deir Siryan in Marjeyoun District. Israeli soldier wounded near Beaufort Castle: An Israeli reservist was "seriously injured" Monday in an explosion in southern Lebanon near Beaufort Castle, in the Nabatieh area, the Israeli army said, according to Haaretz. The military said it was still investigating the incident and that the soldier was hospitalized. About 400,000 displaced Lebanese have returned home since March, minister says: About 400,000 forcibly displaced people in Lebanon, roughly 40% of the more than 1.2 million uprooted since Israel re-escalated its war on March 2, have to their home regions, Social Affairs Minister Haneen Sayed said Monday. The number of people sheltering in reception centers has fallen to 13,000 from 37,000, he said, though many remain unable to return as Israel occupies a strip of southern Lebanon behind the "Yellow Line." Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 26 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,066 killed, with 173,514 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,053 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,406, while 786 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli bombardment, home demolitions across Gaza: Several Palestinians were on Tuesday after an Israeli airstrike targeted a group of people near the Sheikh Radwan junction in Gaza City, according to WAFA. In southern Gaza, Israeli troops carried out four large-scale demolitions of homes and civilian structures in Khan Younis, while artillery shelled northwestern Rafah. In Gaza City, Israeli forces destroyed homes in the Al-Tuffah neighborhood, alongside heavy gunfire in Shujaiya. Israeli strike on displaced Palestinians kills two, wounds 20: An Israeli drone strike on displaced people in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis two Palestinians and wounded more than 20 others Monday, according to medical sources cited by Al Jazeera. Separately, a Palestinian man was shot and killed by Israeli forces in Al-Qarara, northwest of Khan Younis, according to WAFA, bringing Monday's death toll from Israeli attacks across Gaza to at least eight, two of whom were children. Israel shoots and kills 15-year-old Palestinian in West Bank: Israeli forces a 15-year-old in the head and chest on Monday during a raid in el-Bireh, near Ramallah, WAFA reported. The head of the area's governorate called the killing a "clear-cut execution in broad daylight" and said it made a mockery of "institutions that claim to uphold democracy and human rights." B'Tselem, the Israeli human rights organization, issued a report on Monday saying Israeli forces have killed 241 Palestinian children and teenagers in the occupied West Bank since October 7, 2023. Hamas delegation arrives in Cairo to discuss Gaza ceasefire roadmap: A Hamas delegation arrived in Cairo on Tuesday for talks with Egyptian officials and mediators on implementing the Gaza ceasefire agreement and advancing negotiations on the next phase, according to a statement released by the group. Hamas official Taher Al-Nunu said the delegation, led by Zaher Jabarin, will press for an end to "the escalating Israeli violations" in the Gaza Strip, including "the daily killings and assassinations," while demanding that Israel allow the full entry of humanitarian supplies and reconstruction materials and implement the remaining provisions of the Sharm el-Sheikh Agreement. The delegation will also discuss the second phase of the roadmap presented by Nickolay Mladenov, leading up to "full Israeli withdrawal from all of Gaza." Read the latest on Gaza negotiations from Drop Site's Jeremy Scahill and Jawa Ahmad . Committee to Protect Journalists set to narrow journalist definition: The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) will reportedly its definition of who qualifies as a journalist in a move that would broadly exclude slain Palestinian and Lebanese journalists working for government-funded outlets, while journalists from Israel, the U.S., and Ukraine at state-funded or military-embedded outlets would remain classified as journalists. The change follows pressure from the right-wing publication The Free Beacon, which has repeatedly alleged that Palestinian and Lebanese journalists were militants or cited their political views to justify their killings by Israeli forces. Later on Monday, Drop Site News publisher Dr. Nika Soon-Shiong that she had been removed from the CPJ board, after opposing this proposal. Soon-Shiong published an email she sent to the board arguing that the proposal would politicize CPJ's mission, could exclude journalists based on their employer or alleged conduct, and could undermine protections for journalists, particularly those in Gaza. An internal CPJ email shared with Drop Site calls reports that the organization plans to change its definition "false allegations" and "untrue." It says the review, led by CPJ's Middle East and North Africa team, is focused on its documentation of journalists killed in the Israel-Gaza war after some individuals previously listed as journalists were later determined to have been combatants, and is expected to be completed in July. Released Palestinian detainees describe starvation, sleep deprivation at Israel 's Ofer Prison: Released Palestinian detainees days of starvation, sleep deprivation, and humiliation inside Israel's Ofer Prison in interviews conducted by Mohamed Ahmed for Drop Site News. Nasser Ghaleb Mohammed Al-Haj Ahmad, 35, said detainees were denied food, water, sleep, and bathrooms. "If you sleep, you sleep on iron. There is no sleep, no life." Jamal Shukri Mohammed Abu Shanab, 68, said detainees ate only plain yogurt for 10 days and were bound, forced onto their stomachs, and jolted awake whenever they tried to sleep. The International Committee of the Red Cross, which has been denied access to Israeli-held Palestinian detainees since October 7, 2023, said it transferred 13 released Palestinians from the Kerem Abu Salem crossing to the hospital Monday, with more than 9,400 Palestinians, including over 3,200 held without charge, still imprisoned by Israel. Israeli lawmaker says bill to bar Red Cross visits to Palestinian prisoners defeated: Israeli lawmaker Ofer Cassif, the only Jewish member of the anti-occupation Hadash party in the Knesset, on Monday that lawmakers defeated a bill that would have barred the Red Cross from visiting Palestinian detainees in Israeli prisons. Cassif said the measure was intended to prevent the world from seeing "the marks of torture and inhumane conditions" on Palestinian prisoners. He called for the immediate resumption of Red Cross visits to prisons. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Primaries in Colorado on Tuesday: Colorado's Democratic establishment is reportedly increasingly that a progressive wave could reshape Tuesday's primaries, with Politico reporting that Sen. John Hickenlooper is in a "dead heat" with state Sen. Julie Gonzales in Denver and that Rep. Diana DeGette 's campaign is alarmed by internal polling showing her race with progressive challenger Melat Krios tightening. Allies of Sen. Michael Bennet also reportedly acknowledged his gubernatorial race against Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser is closer than expected, per private polling cited by Politico. A last-minute infusion of funds into DeGette's campaign from AIPAC and big tech is discussed in the latest from Ryan Grim , Julian Andreone , and Toby Jaffe for Drop Site, available . Monday 's Supreme Court decisions: Upholds state laws counting late-arriving mail ballots: The Supreme Court 5-4 Monday that election officials may count postmarked mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day, rejecting a Republican National Committee challenge to a Mississippi law and finding it does not conflict with federal law setting Election Day in early November. The ruling, authored by Justice Amy Coney Barrett with two conservatives joining the three liberals in the majority, keeps the Mississippi law and similar measures in 13 other states in effect ahead of November's midterms. Splits on Trump 's power to fire independent agency officials, blocks Fed's Cook ouster but allows FTC firing: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 Monday that President Donald Trump fire Federal Reserve board memberLisa Cook for now, with Chief Justice John Roberts writing that for-cause protections shield the Fed from being treated as "at-will employment." In a separate 6-3 ruling, however, the Court overturned the 1935 precedent Humphrey's Executor v. United States and allowed Trump to remove Federal Trade Commission memberRebecca Kelly Slaughter without cause. Roberts wrote in the Slaughter ruling that "subordinates who exercise the president's power are subject to removal by him." Trump indicated on Truth Social that he would still seek to fire Cook, whom he has accused of committing mortgage fraud. Cook denies the claims. Rejects Trump 's bid to overturn $5 million E. Jean Carroll verdict: The Supreme Court Monday, without explanation or noted dissents, to hear President Donald Trump's appeal of a jury's $5 million finding that he sexually abused writer E. Jean Carroll at a Manhattan department store in the mid-1990s and later defamed her, according to the Associated Press. AOC introduces NDAA amendment that could halt U.S. military aid to Israel: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez(D-N.Y.) an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act on Monday that could effectively halt offensive and defensive U.S. military aid to Israel. The proposal would require U.S. defense transfers to comply with international law and, building on Section 620I of the Foreign Assistance Act, would require the president to affirmatively certify that a recipient isn't restricting U.S.-backed humanitarian aid. Ocasio-Cortez's amendment requires the president to affirmatively certify that the laws banning the restriction of aid are being followed and also requires Congress to authorize the weapons transfers before they can proceed. Ocasio-Cortez has also pursued amendments that focus on the U.S. military's presence in Latin America, requiring the Pentagon to publish a report on its use of military facilities in Puerto Rico, demanding an accounting of human rights violations in Peru between 2022 and 2024 and in Colombia for the last 3 decades, and barring military cooperation with Ecuador's current government. The congresswoman with Drop Site's Julian Andreone on Tuesday about her proposed amendments. Watch. House Rules Committee blocks Massie-Khanna amendment to remove Israel tech provision from NDAA: The House Rules Committee a bipartisan amendment from Reps. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) andRo Khanna(D-Calif.)** that sought to remove a provision expanding U.S.-Israel military technology integration from the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act, meaning it will not receive a House floor vote. The underlying provision, which remains in the NDAA, would deepen U.S.-Israel defense technology cooperation, including joint weapons development and other military collaboration. Progressive Caucus chair Greg Casar to back Massie amendment cutting U.S. military aid to Israel: Rep. Greg Casar(D-Texas), chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, on Monday that he will vote for Rep. Thomas Massie 's amendment to end U.S. taxpayer-funded military aid for Israel, arguing the Israeli government "committed war crimes in Gaza and helped drag America into war with Iran." The amendment would bar funds in the bill from going to Israel and cut Foreign Military Financing by $3.3 billion, though it would not constitute an arms embargo or ban all U.S. arms sales to Israel. Jewish Voice for Peace Action endorses Abdul El-Sayed for Michigan Senate seat: Jewish Voice for Peace Action its first-ever Senate endorsement to Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Monday, citing his consistent stance on human rights and progressive foreign policy. Colorado Supreme Court blocks Democratic redistricting effort: The Colorado Supreme Court a blow Monday to Democratic efforts to redraw the state's congressional maps ahead of 2028, ruling that twin ballot initiatives violated the state constitution's "single subject requirement" because each measure was contingent on the other's passage. Democrats behind the effort said time has run out to gather the roughly 125,000 signatures needed by August 3 to qualify for November's ballot, dealing a setback to a plan that aimed to draw up to three new Democratic-leaning districts as part of the broader national redistricting fight. Rep. Yassamin Ansari calls Israel 's actions in Gaza "genocide," vows to reject AIPAC funding: Rep. Yassamin Ansari of Arizona, the first Iranian American Democrat elected to Congress, Israel's actions in Gaza and Lebanon a "genocide" and pledged to stop accepting money from pro-Israel groups including AIPAC, in an interview with Zeteo on Monday. The shift marks a reversal for Ansari, who won her 2024 primary as a self-described "proud pro-Israel progressive" backed by Democratic Majority for Israel, opposed Sen.Bernie Sanders 's effort to block $20 billion in arms sales to Israel, and voted to sanction the International Criminal Court over its warrants for Israeli leaders. DOJ opens investigation into Sen. Ruben Gallego days after Senate Ethics Committee clears him: The Justice Department has an investigation into Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) stemming from a "whistleblower complaint" out of Southern California related to his use of a political committee's PAC to fund family trips to Miami, Chicago, Disneyland, and Disney World, coming days after the Senate Ethics Committee closed its inquiry into separate sexual misconduct and campaign finance allegations after finding no rule violations. Gallego, who has hired former Biden deputy press secretary Andrew Bates for crisis communications help amid fallout from his public friendship with former Rep. Eric Swalwell , has denied wrongdoing and said the allegations are politically motivated as he weighs a potential 2028 presidential run. NYC Council Member Paladino suggests CIA, FBI should "neutralize" DSA leaders: New York City Council Member Vickie Paladino in a post on Monday that the CIA and FBI once would have "neutralized one way or another" "unabashed revolutionaries" while sharing a post identifying Democratic Socialists of America leadership members. Congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier called the remarks a "thinly veiled call" for the federal government to kill DSA members and demanded Paladino's expulsion from the City Council. Other International News Iraq sets September 30 deadline for Iran-aligned factions to disarm under U.S. pressure: Iraq's government has Iran-aligned armed factions until September 30 to disarm. The deadline was announced ahead of a visit to the U.S. by Iraq's new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi. Iraqi government spokesman Haidar al-Aboudi said Monday that groups possessing weapons would face legal action after that date, which also marks the end of the international anti-ISIS coalition's presence in the country. Two factions, Kataeb Imam Ali and Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have already agreed to turn over administration of their brigades to the state, while others among Iraq's dozens of Iran-aligned factions, some of which attacked U.S. bases during this year's Iran war, have yet to comply, according to AFP and The New Arab. Also on Monday, Iraqi security forces, including the elite Counter-Terrorism Service, 47 people, including lawmakers, senior officials, and prominent politicians, in an anticorruption crackdown ordered by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, raiding homes in Baghdad's Green Zone and other neighborhoods. Iraq's Federal Commission of Integrity said the arrests were based on judicial warrants tied to alleged misappropriation of public funds, with lawmakers' parliamentary immunity lifted beforehand. They follow last month's arrest of Deputy Oil Minister Adnan al-Jumaili and the seizure of roughly $86 million in cash. Russian strikes across Ukraine kill at least eight, including a child: Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine at least eight people and wounded 34 others Monday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, including five killed and 28 wounded in a missile attack on Dnipro and three killed and six wounded, among them a child, in a drone attack on Zaporizhzhia. Additional Russian strikes hit the Sumy, Odesa, Chernihiv, Kherson, and Kharkiv regions. The Kremlin said Monday that Russia's position on a peace deal has remained unchanged since 2024, when Putin said Kyiv must withdraw from four regions Moscow claims and drop its NATO bid. Rubio meets Libyan commander Saddam Haftar: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Monday with Libyan National Army Deputy Commander Saddam Haftar to discuss unification efforts in the country and possible cooperation between the U.S. and Haftar's LNA, according to a State Department readout. The meeting came the same day a new documentary by Evident, Sudan War Monitor, and LightHouse presented new evidence that Haftar has worked with the UAE to facilitate arms and training for Sudan's RSF militia. South Africa deploys police as anti-immigrant groups ' deportation "deadline" sparks fear, business closures: Businesses across South African cities and police were deployed on Tuesday as anti-immigrant protests continued nationwide ahead of a "deadline" anti-immigrant groups have given undocumented foreign nationals to leave, falsely claiming they will otherwise face arrest and deportation, according to Al Jazeera. President Cyril Ramaphosa said the right to protest "does not allow people to threaten or intimidate others, or to engage in acts of vandalism or violence." Weeks of xenophobic violence in the country have killed people from Mozambique, Ethiopia, and Malawi, according to AFP, with thousands of foreign nationals, including some in the country legally, sheltering at consulates or being repatriated by their home countries. UK national security bill could expose journalists to "terrorism" prosecution, legal experts warn: British journalists reporting from countries like Iran could terrorism prosecutions under a UK national security bill expected to complete its final parliamentary stages this week, according to reporting Monday in the Guardian. Legal expert David Anderson warned the bill could criminalize foreign correspondents for obtaining information from sources within state-designated groups because it lacks explicit protections for journalists, and press freedom groups are urging amendments. | Fellow Republicans,
Winning in November doesn't happen by chance.
It happens with Republicans showing up, knocking on doors, and talking to voters.
That's why the Massachusetts Republican Party is launching the MassGOP Summer Victory Tour: a statewide series of grassroots trainings on campaign fundamentals and coordinated Days of Action to build the volunteer army that will power Republican victories.
Doors Knocked = Voters Reached = Wins in November
It's really that simple.
Whether you've knocked 5,000 doors or none at all, we'll give you the tools, training, and confidence to get involved immediately.
Training dates and registration information are below. Please register in advance so we can prepare materials and organize teams. And don't come alone!
Bring a friend, neighbor, or fellow Republican who's ready to help take Massachusetts in a new direction.
Our candidates are doing their part.
Now it's our turn.
See you out there.
To Victory, Haley Haley Jones Executive Director Massachusetts Republican Party

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

Make your first gift today and receive a FREE "God's Children Are Not For Sale" t-shirt as our thank-you. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Peter, I want to start with two simple words. Thank you. Thank you for caring about children you may never meet. Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold. Because that is exactly what is happening. Every day. God's children are not for sale. And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth. When you make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation today, we'll send you a FREE white "God's Children Are Not For Sale" t-shirt as our thank-you. | | | | | | | | This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store. You can't buy it online. It was created exclusively for supporters of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say: "No more." Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters. A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity. And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. Most of all Peter, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself. A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold. Families were being torn apart. Lives were being destroyed. I couldn't forget it. I couldn't stay silent. I kept asking myself one question: "What if it were my child?" That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film Sound of Freedom. Not for fame. Not for awards. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed. Studios walked away. People told us to give up. But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option. And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Our mission is simple: To stop the sale of God's children. Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back. Jesus said, "Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14) Every child is precious in God's eyes. Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth. And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them When you make your first gift today, you help: Prevent exploitation by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children. Support intervention efforts by equipping trusted partners working to help rescue children trapped in exploitation. Educate parents and communities about the warning signs traffickers use to target children. Raise awareness so more people understand the reality of this crisis. Advocate for stronger protections for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers. This is how change happens. One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet. Today, that person can be you. Will you make your first gift now? Choose your shirt size and select a color. And know that your generosity will help protect vulnerable children and bring hope to those who need it most. Thank you for caring and for standing with vulnerable children. Thank you for choosing action over silence. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. | Peter, my students tell me that I can get a little long-winded. I don't want to take up too much of your time, so I'll do my best to get to the point.

This summer has already been busy for our campaign. We've been traveling across IA-01, meeting voters, and sharing our vision for a better future. Some days it's hot, some days it rains, but we're out there because we believe our communities deserve a representative who will show up and fight for them.

And I have to tell you, I'm incredibly proud of what we've built together. Since launching this campaign last year, we've brought together people from all walks of life around a simple idea: _That Iowa deserves better._ Now, I need your support to keep up this amazing momentum.

Our end-of-quarter FEC deadline is at midnight, and we're working to reach our $30,000 goal before the clock runs out. After this deadline, our fundraising numbers for the last three months will go public, and I want to show Mariannette Miller-Meeks we have what it takes to win. Will you make a donation right now to help us close the final gap before midnight? Chip in >> [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cb-q2-2026?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134312609/630839366/-2009658230?refcode=em26_260630_EOQ6_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260630_EOQ6_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=d981665a-9474-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkOTgxNjY1YS05NDc0LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b3mP0jkfAFYZVoLRruh9zedKRWc98XyZeHo6MDRx57E=)

Okay, maybe that wasn't quite as short as I intended. Old habits die hard. But thank you for taking the time to read this, and thank you for being part of this campaign. It means more to me than you know.

Thank you,

Christina

Peter,
Today is the Primary Election Day!
If your ballot is still sitting on your kitchen counter, it’s too late to return it by mail but there’s still time to make your voice heard! You can drop off your ballot at a drop box or voting center by 7:00 p.m. tonight, or vote in-person at a voting center today by 7:00 pm.
As Colorado’s Secretary of State, I’ve worked to protect and strengthen our elections so every eligible voter can make their voice heard. And as I run to become Colorado’s next Attorney General, I’m asking you to take part in the democratic process that makes our state so strong.
Participating in our democracy matters. Here in Colorado, we’ve made voting accessible, secure, and convenient for every voter. Let’s continue that tradition by showing up and making our voices heard today.
Find your closest ballot box or voting center here! [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/VIP.html]
Let’s get out the vote, Peter!
– Jena Griswold
Candidate for Attorney General

If you've been denied healthcare, "don't qualify" for benefits, and are tired of politicians giving vague answers for why our working class is being crushed, _I have the answer.****_**Let 's call it what it really is: rampant, unchecked corporate greed.**
**And it is all fueled by representatives like my opponent, who take thousands in Corporate interest money:**

body:
---
Derek, the Supreme Court just gave billionaires the green light to spend even more in our elections. The DNC took up the fight. We did all that could be done, including arguing at the Supreme Court. But the Court overturned its own precedent to rule for Republicans and big money in politics. [**Now I’m urgently asking you to chip in to the DNC Fight Fund to help Democrats be ready for the coming avalanche of billionaire cash.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dnc-email-2026-june-fight-fund?refcode=em_20260630_7812_fr&amount=7&refcode2=7816_22930333_SVSjPB&akid=7816%2E22930333%2ESVSjPB) In a landmark case, the DNC argued to stop JD Vance and the Republicans from changing campaign finance rules in their favor. Conservatives on the Court just sided with the Republicans who appointed them. So now I’m asking every single person reading this email to stop what you’re doing, dig deep, and chip in to the DNC Fight Fund. Because here’s what’s coming next. The Supreme Court’s ruling allows billionaires to funnel money through the Republican Party to spend in coordination with their candidates, carving a clear path around contribution limits. Republicans did this for one simple reason: they can’t compete with us in grassroots donations — so they made it easier for the wealthiest few to tip the scales back in their favor. The odds are now stacked higher against grassroots donors like you. Corruption is far easier. But the last thing we should do is throw in the towel. If we band together instead of giving up — _if we get a surge of grassroots support like never before_ — then we’ll make Republicans regret messing with the rules. We’ll prove that when they try to undermine our impact, we’ll dig that much deeper. **Greetings, Alaskans: ** **Alaska's potential is real, and so is the work ahead. We have the resources, the people, and the resolve to build something stronger, and this race is about making sure that will happen in every corner of our state. AND ALASKANS ARE GETTING JAZZED! New supporters are coming on board every day! Those that hesitated to pick a candidate earlier, are excitedly joining us in support.**** ****This week, new supporters came on board as we took our message on the road and across the airways. From Dutch Harbor and Unalaska to the Soldotna Senior Center. From fish camps to city centers, we've been meeting Alaskans where they are, listening to what families need. On education: Alaska can do better, and with the right leadership and focus, I believe we will. Roads, airports, and ports: we can do better. Fish and game: we can do better. More affordable living: we can do better. No problem is insurmountable. With effective leadership, an action plan, and working together, we can move mountains!**** ****Please know not only does your support mean the world to us, but the very message that resonates with you, needs to get out across our huge state! It takes dollars to make that happen, and we're counting on you! Once you donate, be sure to scroll down for the full week in photos, updates, and where we're headed next.**
**Your biggest advocate,**

clean_body: Shelley has been everywhere this week, and she's just getting started. | | | | | | | Proven Leadership. Integrity. Real Solutions. Greetings, Alaskans: Alaska's potential is real, and so is the work ahead. We have the resources, the people, and the resolve to build something stronger, and this race is about making sure that will happen in every corner of our state. AND ALASKANS ARE GETTING JAZZED! New supporters are coming on board every day! Those that hesitated to pick a candidate earlier, are excitedly joining us in support. This week, new supporters came on board as we took our message on the road and across the airways. From Dutch Harbor and Unalaska to the Soldotna Senior Center. From fish camps to city centers, we've been meeting Alaskans where they are, listening to what families need. On education: Alaska can do better, and with the right leadership and focus, I believe we will. Roads, airports, and ports: we can do better. Fish and game: we can do better. More affordable living: we can do better. No problem is insurmountable. With effective leadership, an action plan, and working together, we can move mountains! Please know not only does your support mean the world to us, but the very message that resonates with you, needs to get out across our huge state! It takes dollars to make that happen, and we're counting on you! Once you donate, be sure to scroll down for the full week in photos, updates, and where we're headed next. Your biggest advocate, Shelley HughesRepublican Candidate for Governor of the Great State of Alaska p.s. The August Primary is just 7 weeks away and we need your support now more than ever! Our current target is $10,000 for digital ads. Help us get there! Whether you have $10 to give or $10,000, Blake and I are very grateful for you and your support. | ~~ "Donate Today!" | Alaska Needs Dependable, Experienced Leadership With a Plan "Alaska has incredible potential—and real challenges that require experienced, conservative leadership willing to get to work. I’ve seen firsthand what Alaskans are up against: the high cost of living, the need for opportunity in every region of our state, and the importance of making government more accountable and focused on priorities that matter to families. I’m ready to fight for our state. Five weeks from today, voters in VA-01 go to the polls.
And midnight tonight is our last end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before that moment arrives.
I won't sugarcoat it: What we raise tonight determines the scale of our campaign in these final five weeks. More resources means more ads, more doors knocked, more voters reached. Less means tough choices about what we can afford to do between now and August 4th.
Rob Wittman has 18 years of name recognition, millions in corporate PAC backing, and an establishment machine working for him. We have something better — a grassroots movement of voters who are fed up and ready for real leadership.
But grassroots movements need fuel. Tonight is when we fill the tank.
Here's what's on the line: Healthcare costs that keep rising while Wittman protects his donors. Social Security that Wittman won't defend — literally faking a phone call rather than answer whether he'd protect it. Eighteen years of a congressman who has served himself instead of this district.
We can end it. August 4th. But only if we have the resources to reach every voter between now and then.
Tonight is not just another fundraising deadline. Tonight is the last chance to build the war chest that wins this race.
Midnight tonight. Final EOQ before Election Day. Chip in $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can and let's head into the final five weeks ready to win. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melltull4congress]

Peter,
Down here in the South, when someone says something so ridiculous you can't decide whether to laugh at them or cry out of embarrassment for them, we just shake our heads and say, "Bless their heart."
My opponent is bragging that the Trump endorsement is the "most powerful endorsement in the world" and that he is the "greatest president this country has ever had." I beg to differ -- and so do the Louisiana moms paying more on their grocery and utility bills, the Louisiana farmers who lost out on $2 billion in exports, the Louisiana residents and the Louisiana truck drivers and workers who paid $4 and $5 for diesel.
That "blessing" might help her skip through this runoff, but come November, it will be the downfall of her campaign.
---
| [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0015fvfYh885ePzuitRluHPP9J39caURFkreRsLs13SqTJTGYyc_BY8eoY6cMmZvmKYbf_-sUo3M0Fz8su9zokxgid1BoObaLUklvzncS3GsYTnRv7-gLlGfeX8wkddNJBKok2bZHbYuyoJIU4P6d9XvwUohYMQUnej7drA_FJrFxYYP8KV0DWBs652fwQem9EpbygHdeCzFFCsDI_P-k64MuTjsmZGVBHJ&c=s85SVIx76CA0EIHad0skQq-bAJ2StvLeyHdw9DMbWXgG4Wj3BVUIJw==&ch=DZHBbyj6FX_WSA_HvUOpqURQtGruFTeDCx58h6TXwlFlq7qp9lSOZA==)
---
She may have locked down the MAGA base, but his endorsement is driving away every single Louisianian alienated by: astronomical healthcare, unlivable wages, the release of those Epstein files, and the gas prices shouldered on us by the Iran-war.
I hear this anger every day -- in my truck on back roads, in town halls, and in churches. Folks don't need a pollster to tell them what they're living through.
The media says Louisiana is "too red," but plenty of Republicans tell me they're voting for me because they're done with the lies and corruption. And they're done being told who to vote for because of who the candidate is friends with, instead of what they've done.
My name is Jamie Davis, and I'm the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Louisiana. I'm a successful businessman and third-generation row-crop farmer working over 3000 acres (the same land my grandpa worked as a sharecropper) -- I just shocked MAGA by cleaning house in this runoff with 80% of the vote.
And let's remember: Trump didn't back Julia Letlow out of love. He wanted to punish Bill Cassidy for voting to impeach him. And about 100,000 Republicans still chose Cassidy over Trump's pick. This November, those voters are coming our way.
And that's gonna be a blessing for everybody.
[If you can bless this campaign with $25, $10, or even just $5, before our EOQ deadline at 11:59 PM ET tonight it will go directly toward reaching those voters who are repulsed by the Trump regime.
