Peter,

Today is the last day of the quarter. No spin, no manufactured panic. Just
the truth: we're short of the donor goal that supports COURIER's
reporting, and we have hours left to reach our goal.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20260630_EOQ&akid=91%2E344797%2El2PXWi ]We're still hundreds short of our 5,000 donor goal.
We're not going to dress that up. If COURIER's reporting has been worth
something to you, tonight is the night it counts to show your
support.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1006&refcode=20260630_EOQ&akid=91%2E344797%2El2PXWi ]Chip in $27

It's been another surreal month in Trump's America.

But it's also been a month of incredible journalism here at COURIER.
Across our local newsrooms in states like Michigan, Virginia, and Iowa,
our reporters:

* Tracked the data center buildout spreading across the country and what
it means for families' utility bills
* Reported on rural hospital closures and what they mean for the
families who depend on them
* Covered the affordability squeeze hitting households every day
* Followed redistricting all the way to the Virginia Supreme Court

That's the work your support pays for. Not access journalism. Not
billionaire-owned both-sidesism.

Vital reporting in battleground states where reliable sources for news are
hard to come by if they exist at all.

We don't answer to Trump or fear of retribution. We answer to readers like
you who support our work when they can.

That's the whole model, and it only works if enough people decide
independent local journalism is worth funding before it disappears.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1007&refcode=20260630_EOQ&akid=91%2E344797%2El2PXWi ]What we raise each quarter determines whether or not we
can sustain our work. If you can, please support COURIER with a donation
of any amount before midnight:

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1008&refcode=20260630_EOQ&akid=91%2E344797%2El2PXWi ]DONATE BEFORE MIDNIGHT

We don't do guilt trips. Just the truth: independent journalism doesn't
survive without people willing to pay for it. If that's you, tonight's the
night, and we're grateful for whatever you can do.

In solidarity,
The COURIER Team

name: Troy Carter
subject: I could be Louisiana’s last Black Congressman
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE DSCC OF LA
body:
if this happens, and all signs say it will, I stand to be...
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001CJbEYyXZ7YFuXFUoneOaLw5yAilbAX7owHNYaNjIp_WtYsyvv18-7EUCLAHoJFHCU0_bi7IiznKU0ppjYqf4TZvSmE1-87NQkDFCPTwVMpH2m1y4ZBsttGuq9gk8enLHBA4ECFE7jSA_Tbt0GIOn3j1yazIbT6AaVXLHf86KfBCrZZyPYGKOtkUKJp9uld-bn-x0dmmX348WhyScZh1Ek8pb9JmwH0Hy7PQ8lmB0vfc=&c=tgqEoMqAKcpNmzlymJ_bLf8aqAuddr_YWkg38Hg1crVUdwCzVonY6A==&ch=KBIDHosHeEBpSvLuQL9yM8BJNxAd1oIRE4E7T5VPh8h_UeV5a45K0g==)
---
| Peter,
My name is Troy Carter and I proudly represent Louisiana's 2nd congressional district, the last remaining majority-Black district in the state.
And if MAGA has its way, the district I represent will be the last ever majority-Black district in Louisiana. I could very well be Louisiana's last Black Congressman.
By now, you've heard about what MAGA did to Black voters in Louisiana.
In April, the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. Then MAGA declared a state of emergency to cancel our election, tossed out tens of thousands of ballots, and rammed through a brand-new map that erased one of our majority-Black districts -- the seat held by my colleague and dear friend Cleo Fields.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001CJbEYyXZ7YFuXFUoneOaLw5yAilbAX7owHNYaNjIp_WtYsyvv18-7EUCLAHoJFHCU0_bi7IiznKU0ppjYqf4TZvSmE1-87NQkDFCPTwVMpH2m1y4ZBsttGuq9gk8enLHBA4ECFE7jSA_Tbt0GIOn3j1yazIbT6AaVXLHf86KfBCrZZyPYGKOtkUKJp9uld-bn-x0dmmX348WhyScZh1Ek8pb9JmwH0HyddWdDAYfvL4=&c=tgqEoMqAKcpNmzlymJ_bLf8aqAuddr_YWkg38Hg1crVUdwCzVonY6A==&ch=KBIDHosHeEBpSvLuQL9yM8BJNxAd1oIRE4E7T5VPh8h_UeV5a45K0g==)
---
But that's not the full story.
While they were debating the map that wiped out Cleo's district, MAGA had a second map waiting in the wings -- one that went even further. It eliminated my district too. Then Black voters showed up. They flooded the Capitol, furious at being stripped of their representation. And facing that kind of heat, MAGA blinked.
And then MAGA pulled a bait and switch. They benched the map that killed my district and passed the one that eliminated Cleo's -- and the moment the ink was dry, they sprang the trap:
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001CJbEYyXZ7YFuXFUoneOaLw5yAilbAX7owHNYaNjIp_WtYsyvv18-7EUCLAHoJFHCU0_bi7IiznKU0ppjYqf4TZvSmE1-87NQkDFCPTwVMpH2m1y4ZBsttGuq9gk8enLHBA4ECFE7jSA_Tbt0GIOn3j1yazIbT6AaVXLHf86KfBCrZZyPYGKOtkUKJp9uld-bn-x0dmmX348WhyScZh1Ek8pb9JmwH0HyE_z_v6SlJKY=&c=tgqEoMqAKcpNmzlymJ_bLf8aqAuddr_YWkg38Hg1crVUdwCzVonY6A==&ch=KBIDHosHeEBpSvLuQL9yM8BJNxAd1oIRE4E7T5VPh8h_UeV5a45K0g==)
---
MAGA activists immediately challenged the very map their own legislature had just passed, claiming my district was an "illegal racial gerrymander." It was a setup. They didn't want to vote to eliminate my seat in the open, so they're trying to get a court to do their dirty work behind closed doors -- so MAGA can wipe out Black representation in Louisiana without any more blood on their hands.
We've been here before. I'm one of five Black people elected to serve in Congress, the fourth since Reconstruction. The first, John Willis Menard, was denied his seat in Congress, challenged by that period's MAGA movement.
I'm not backing down from this fight. But I can't win it alone. Right now, MAGA's lawyers are working to convince a court to do what they were too scared to do in the open: erase my district and silence the Black voters who sent me to Congress. They are betting that we'll be too tired, too distracted, or too broken to fight back. Let's prove them wrong.
[That's where you come in, Peter. We need a surge in support of Democrats from across the nation to help us fight for Louisiana's last majority-Black district. Can I count on you to chip in $50, $25, or even $15, split between my campaign and the Louisiana Democrats, to stand with every Black voter in Louisiana who refuses to let MAGA drag this state back to the Jim Crow era?](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001CJbEYyXZ7YFuXFUoneOaLw5yAilbAX7owHNYaNjIp_WtYsyvv18-7EUCLAHoJFHC4c9NVYJ6nqnx23AXtCt74mMh-fF1v1HIkUgKK9pmJUBIgMm-MuIUd6fP5DWxLWPzs1ckiuAkwOPSx-qadODP1wDj6tUDVM_UjMxZ7TxCUWUwGnInoESsph79sC9M8VG7LvkEckFklH4Li84ktxUZAk3B5xxWM-Crn3Z2QOTtUXlY-RCYbj0eNA==&c=tgqEoMqAKcpNmzlymJ_bLf8aqAuddr_YWkg38Hg1crVUdwCzVonY6A==&ch=KBIDHosHeEBpSvLuQL9yM8BJNxAd1oIRE4E7T5VPh8h_UeV5a45K0g==)

clean_body: if this happens, and all signs say it will, I stand to be... | | | | | == | Peter, My name is Troy Carter and I proudly represent Louisiana's 2nd congressional district, the last remaining majority-Black district in the state. And if MAGA has its way, the district I represent will be the last ever majority-Black district in Louisiana. I could very well be Louisiana's last Black Congressman. By now, you've heard about what MAGA did to Black voters in Louisiana. In April, the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. Then MAGA declared a state of emergency to cancel our election, tossed out tens of thousands of ballots, and rammed through a brand-new map that erased one of our majority-Black districts -- the seat held by my colleague and dear friend Cleo Fields. | == But that's not the full story. While they were debating the map that wiped out Cleo's district, MAGA had a second map waiting in the wings -- one that went even further. It eliminated my district too. Then Black voters showed up. They flooded the Capitol, furious at being stripped of their representation. And facing that kind of heat, MAGA blinked. And then MAGA pulled a bait and switch. They benched the map that killed my district and passed the one that eliminated Cleo's -- and the moment the ink was dry, they sprang the trap: | == MAGA activists immediately challenged the very map their own legislature had just passed, claiming my district was an "illegal racial gerrymander." It was a setup. They didn't want to vote to eliminate my seat in the open, so they're trying to get a court to do their dirty work behind closed doors -- so MAGA can wipe out Black representation in Louisiana without any more blood on their hands. We've been here before. I'm one of five Black people elected to serve in Congress, the fourth since Reconstruction. The first, John Willis Menard, was denied his seat in Congress, challenged by that period's MAGA movement. I'm not backing down from this fight. But I can't win it alone. Right now, MAGA's lawyers are working to convince a court to do what they were too scared to do in the open: erase my district and silence the Black voters who sent me to Congress. They are betting that we'll be too tired, too distracted, or too broken to fight back. Last Tuesday, all of Zohran Mamdani-endorsed candidates won--the mayor went three-for-three in congressional endorsements and five-for-five in state legislative endorsements. His clean sweep offers a glimpse of how a leader can reshape an entire party--and it shows why it's time for the left to get behind a possible presidential run by Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Because as Mamdani's kingmaker status demonstrates, there's almost nothing that can expand a faction's appeal within a party more than the head of the party being from that faction.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1Jl7529uat3aobC1pXwhS_cBGM1GGdNPU2z_VRw2iA4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=204284121)
That's not to say that Mamdani's support was the only variable in the left's wins on Tuesday. NY-DSA's door-to-door organizing capacity is incredibly important. Voter backlash against incumbents' AIPAC-fueled support for Israel was a major factor. And more broadly, the Democratic base's rage at the failure of party elites to stop Trump has shifted the terrain on which all insurgent primary challenges are playing out.
But Mamdani was unquestionably a key driver in these races. That is particularly clear in Claire Valdez's lopsided victory in NY-7 over Antonio Reynoso, a former insurgent himself with a record of genuine progressive accomplishments whose platform was virtually identical to Valdez's. The most important distinguishing factor in that race was Mamdani's endorsement. It seemed like every Valdez mailer had Mamdani's smiling face on it. And it made all the difference.
The lesson here is that, at least within their particular jurisdiction, a chief executive becomes the leader of their party. And when you're the chief executive and leader of your party, as Donald Trump [put it](https://substack.com/redirect/48f23cf7-c492-4629-8fcc-ba4dfc23f01a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "Everyone wants to be [your] friend." This bandwagon effect doesn't always materialize--nobody is arguing that Chicago's beleaguered Mayor Brandon Johnson is remaking that city's politics in his image. But the attentional advantages of an effective chief executive mean that when such a leader has a clear vision for where their party needs to go and explicitly communicates that vision to party members, they can remake their party.
We saw this dynamic clearly in Trump's consolidation of the GOP. Over just a few cycles, he shattered the Republican establishment and turned it into a vessel for the MAGA movement. We even saw Biden, despite his obvious frailties, engender a trace of this--it's no accident that insurgent progressive primary wins largely trailed off during his term, because in general, the average party member wants to be with their leader.
And that's exactly what we're seeing today with Mamdani's success in reshaping the Democratic establishment in New York City. _Politico_ summed up this dynamic well in an [article](https://substack.com/redirect/12dc0c9a-a894-48dc-942a-ef774271b98a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about how centrist Democrats "are freaking out" that progressives are "becoming more mainstream as they keep winning--reshaping the Democratic Party." Or as Liam Kerr, head of the Manchin-glazing WelcomePAC, put it: "Centrist Democrats, normie Democrats, need to realize we're the insurgents, and they're the new establishment."
That is, of course, DSA's goal: to create a new, pro-working class, anti-oligarchy establishment to run the Democratic Party. And Mamdani's new undisputed role as kingmaker shows that taking a big swing for the top executive spot can pay such outsized dividends toward that end that it's worth the risk.
In hindsight, this all seems obvious. But it's worth remembering that it was not so clear at the beginning of Mamdani's mayoral campaign. Many of NY-DSA's members in office [advocated against](https://substack.com/redirect/28a60cbf-d8e7-4a34-8c50-c9a887cdd86f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) endorsing Mamdani, arguing that the potential downsides of his run were too great and the movement should continue focusing on building up its ranks of lower-level elected officials.
Many on the left today have a similar analysis when it comes to the 2028 presidential campaign. It's time for us to exorcise those doubts. There's simply nothing that matters more than a leftist winning the Democratic presidential nomination. It matters for our chances of defeating MAGA--because the Democratic Party's best shot to beat Trump's successor is with a candidate who embraces real economic populism. It matters for our substantive goals--because, as Trump has demonstrated, the US presidency has accumulated essentially imperial power to pursue an agenda through executive and administrative action. Perhaps most of all, it matters for the left's project of remaking the Democratic Party into one that can actually tackle the obscene inequality, rampant corruption, escalating climate crisis, and other existential challenges of our era--because as Mamdani's mayoralty has demonstrated in New York City, if a leftist can become the leader of the national Democratic Party, the median Democratic voter will follow.
That's where Ocasio-Cortez comes in.
Of course, AOC is not the only progressive who could plausibly run for president. Congressman Ro Khanna has been boldly supporting populists across the country, calling out the sclerosis of Democrats' congressional leadership, and leading the charge in prosecuting the case against the Epstein class. Senator Chris Van Hollen, who has been a courageous voice against Israeli apartheid, also recently expressed an interest in at least exploring a presidential campaign. And I, for one, would be all in for a third Bernie Sanders run.
But the chances of that materializing at Sanders's age--he will be 86 in 2028--seem close to nil, which is likely why Sanders has been working so hard to build up the next generation of left leadership. And though nobody can ever quite fill his shoes, there is a clear inheritor of Sanders's role as standard-bearer for the US left: AOC.
Much of the chatter about AOC's political future has focused on [whether she should run for president or challenge Chuck Schumer](https://substack.com/redirect/167f01ab-2d3c-4c87-8372-4bee12de56f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Senate. But at this point, challenging Schumer is a waste of her talents. Schumer's [favorability](https://substack.com/redirect/fb1a9058-0b8f-4540-90c6-c4c15ee62b40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among New Yorkers sits at just 38 percent, the Democratic base is furious at him for his capitulations to Trump, and the issue most central to his political identity--unquestioning loyalty to the Israeli government--has become toxic among Democratic primary voters. You don't need an AOC to take him out--there are numerous other progressive leaders in the state who could do so.
By contrast, it's hard to imagine anyone on the left being in a better position for a presidential run than AOC is right now. She's one of the most effective communicators in the Democratic Party. She's one of the strongest grassroots [fundraisers](https://substack.com/redirect/2e8cf00b-09c0-4f92-8446-4c7dfa80edd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Congress. She's one of the most [popular](https://substack.com/redirect/8266a2ca-b6a3-4500-912e-4607843942db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) politicians in the country. And she is uniquely positioned to build the kind of increasingly potent Democratic primary coalition--young people, Latinos, and working-class voters--that powered other major anti-establishment victories, from Mamdani to James Talarico in Texas. This goes beyond identity politics--it's not just that AOC is young, Latina, and working class. It's that she can genuinely and compellingly speak to the experiences, fears, and aspirations of these constituencies.
What she isn't, at this point, is clearly set on pursuing a presidential campaign in 2028. When asked by David Axelrod if she was running, she [answered](https://substack.com/redirect/dcdf90f3-8882-42e4-8eeb-91bc469042f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "My ambition is to change this country. Presidents come and go. Senate, House seats, elected officials come and go. But single-payer healthcare is forever... I make decisions by waking up in the morning, looking out the window and observing the conditions of this country. And saying what move or what decision can I make today that is going to get us closer to that future, stronger, faster, better than yesterday."
This response was [celebrated](https://substack.com/redirect/58b356ec-7fa9-41a3-a2da-292171f20644?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) online as a piece of rhetoric, and rightly so--it's a phenomenal answer. But as a statement of actual political strategy, it's a little off. If you want single-payer healthcare, there's nothing that could have a greater impact than electing a president who will actually fight to pass single-payer healthcare. And there's nobody in a stronger position right now to be that president than AOC, if she chooses to run.
That's not to say she is perfect. She's a politician, and none of us will agree with all her choices. I personally found her recent [explanation](https://substack.com/redirect/833ca441-5a0c-43d5-a537-b99b2f51a5d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for supporting Hakeem Jeffries as the Democratic leader in the House frustrating. And she made mistakes in the 2024 campaign--others have called for her to [apologize](https://substack.com/redirect/5ada3c9f-a92e-41b7-b854-b88a4e8fa701?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for whitewashing Kamala Harris's Gaza stance during her speech at the DNC, and as someone who [worked](https://substack.com/redirect/b1a5982a-8daa-4e44-8f46-23f45de9fbcf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to oust Biden from the Democratic ticket, I was upset when she (and other progressives) threw him a lifeline after his debate fiasco. Needless to say, the left will have to hold her to [account](https://substack.com/redirect/5ada3c9f-a92e-41b7-b854-b88a4e8fa701?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like any elected leader.
But given the upsides of an AOC presidency, those of us on the left should be urging her to run. If our ultimate aim is to reshape the Democratic Party into a force that can defeat the authoritarian right and transform this country for the better, the struggle for the White House isn't a distraction. It's perhaps the most important political fight of our lifetimes--and AOC can win it.

In a 6-3 decision made just hours ago, the Court struck down federal limits on how much political parties can spend in coordination with their candidates. **That's another guardrail gone** , making it even easier for wealthy donors and special interests to flood our elections with money. Let's call this what it is: **a gift to the people who already have the loudest voices in American politics – billionaires and Super PACs.** I've never believed elections should be won by whoever has the richest friends, but by earning the trust of your neighbors. Today's ruling makes it even harder for grassroots campaigns to compete while giving billionaires and corporate interests another way to buy influence in Washington. I’m not going to take this renegade court’s order standing still. We can and will work to legally override this in Congress. In a 6-3 decision made just hours ago, the Court struck down federal limits on how much political parties can spend in coordination with their candidates. That's another guardrail gone , making it even easier for wealthy donors and special interests to flood our elections with money. Let's call this what it is: a gift to the people who already have the loudest voices in American politics – billionaires and Super PACs. I've never believed elections should be won by whoever has the richest friends, but by earning the trust of your neighbors. Today's ruling makes it even harder for grassroots campaigns to compete while giving billionaires and corporate interests another way to buy influence in Washington. I’m not going to take this renegade court’s order standing still. We can and will work to legally override this in Congress. clean_body: Tonight at midnight, our Q2 report locks in. The DCCC will see every dollar — or every dollar we didn't raise. Peter, Tonight at midnight, it's over. Our Q2 FEC fundraising deadline closes. I need you to understand what that means. The DCCC has officially named NC-03 one of their top targets for 2026. They have a fundraising page built specifically against me. They have outside groups on standby, opposition researchers digging through my record, and liberal donors across the country ready to write big checks the moment they see an opening. Tonight's report is how they decide if that opening exists. A strong number tonight tells them one thing: this seat is locked down, this campaign is ready, and Eastern North Carolina will not be flipped without a fight they cannot win. A weak number tells them something else entirely — and they will spend accordingly. I refuse to give them that confidence! As a doctor, I was trained to act before a situation becomes critical. Right now, with hours left on the clock, this is that moment. We do not get a second chance at this deadline. Whatever we raise by midnight tonight is the number that defines where we stand heading into the most critical stretch of this campaign. Peter, I am proud to have grassroots conservatives like you who understand what's at stake and show up when it matters most. The DCCC thinks NC-03 is a hot seat they can flip. They think our conservative majority in Eastern North Carolina is vulnerable. They think their D.C. money machine can come in here and buy this district right out from under us. They clearly don't know the people I represent. But I need you to prove that tonight — before midnight — with a contribution that shows up on tomorrow's report and sends Hakeem Jeffries a message he won't forget. Every dollar counts. name: Vanessa Enoch for Congress
subject: Midnight Tonight: We Can't Do This Without You
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer
body:
At midnight tonight, our federal fundraising deadline comes to an end, and the numbers we report will show whether our campaign...

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | Hello Peter,
**Today is the day.**
At **midnight tonight** , our federal fundraising deadline comes to an end, and the numbers we report will show whether our campaign has the strength to compete against a well-funded incumbent.
This campaign has never been powered by corporate PACs or billionaire donors. It has always been powered by people like you—neighbors who believe Ohio's 8th District deserves leadership that listens, works hard, and fights for everyday families.Every contribution made before midnight helps us:
* Reach more voters across Butler, Hamilton, Miami, Darke, and Preble counties.
* Keep our field organizers and volunteers in communities across the district.
* Print campaign literature, place signs, and expand our voter outreach.
* Build the grassroots movement we need to win this race.

Washington is working for the powerful while too many Ohio families are working harder than ever just to get by. We need leaders who will fight for affordable healthcare, good-paying jobs, quality education, stronger infrastructure, and an economy that works for everyone—not just those at the top.
But none of that happens unless we have the resources to reach voters.
**If you've been waiting for the right time to help, this is it.**
Whether you can give [**$10, $25, $50, $100, or any amount**](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=f3b8911a75&e=c6e7dff14c) , your donation today will help us finish this reporting period as strongly as possible.Every dollar given before midnight counts.
Please make your contribution now and help us send a message that this campaign is growing, our movement is strong, and the people of Ohio's 8th District are ready for new leadership.
Thank you for believing in this campaign and for standing with me. Together, we can build a future that works for everyone.
With gratitude,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Candidate for U.S. Congress, Ohio's 8th District
**P.S.** The deadline is **midnight tonight**. Once the clock runs out, this reporting period closes. If you're able, please make your contribution today and help us finish strong.With gratitude,
Paid for by the Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer.

name: Jeff, Team Cooper (via Cooper Victory Fund)
subject: New SCOTUS ruling could allow the GOP to try to buy this seat.
body:
Experts were already predicting this would be the first billion-dollar Senate race in history. Today, the Supreme Court guaranteed it.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6532?source=&t=1&akid=1733%2E124072%2EkuFIee)
| | | |
---
Peter, this morning’s Supreme Court decision is the **biggest change to campaign finance law since Citizens United.**
The National Republican Senatorial Committee and JD Vance sued to strike down federal limits on coordinated spending, and they just won.
**The far-right majority ruled that from this day forward, there are virtually ZERO limits on how much money national political parties can funnel to their candidates.**
Here’s what that means: Nothing – truly, _nothing_ – is stopping the Republican Party from investing as much as they want to try to defeat Roy in North Carolina and buy this seat for our opponent in this race, who also happens to be the former chairman of the RNC.
**[If we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate. The stakes couldn’t be higher, so I have to ask: Before tonight’s end-of-quarter deadline, will you chip in what you can to help us fight back against the GOP and flip this seat blue?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk721_v1&amount=5&t=8&akid=1733%2E124072%2EkuFIee)**
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk721_v1&amount=5&t=9&akid=1733%2E124072%2EkuFIee)
---
With GOP super PACs already pouring nearly $100 million so far into North Carolina, experts were predicting this would be the first billion-dollar Senate race in history. Today, the Supreme Court basically guaranteed it.
The Republican Party is going to dump obscene amounts of money into attack ads, voter contact efforts and more – and their dollars go further than super PACs. This surge in dark money could wipe out any advantages we _think_ we have in this race.
**We need an immediate groundswell of grassroots support to help us fight back – or else we could be drowned out by a flood of dark money at the worst possible time.**
**[Peter, will you rush $5 or as much as you can spare right away to ensure we can compete with the GOP, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats before our midnight FEC deadline?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk721_v1&amount=5&t=10&akid=1733%2E124072%2EkuFIee)**

I’m proud to have Senator Martin Heinrich’s support. Help us build a winning campaign for November.

I’m honored to share that I won the Democratic nomination for New Mexico Commissioner of Public Lands earlier this month. **This is a huge win for public lands across New Mexico. Now, we’re on to the general election and we need your help.** Senator Martin Heinrich endorsed our campaign on day one because he knows what is at stake. I was proud to serve as his Political Director and Deputy Campaign Manager, and throughout my career, I have worked to protect New Mexico’s natural resources and fight for the communities that depend on them. name: Team Clark
subject: It's time to stand up.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Clark for Wisconsin
body:
https://www.everyaction.com/ [https://www.everyaction.com/]
Peter,
Back in May, Republican Candidate Michael Alfonso (son-in-law of Trump DOT Secretary Sean Duffy) posted a big fiat fib on his Facebook Page claiming that Fred Clark "hates the Second Amendment". Fred has hunted these Northwoods for decades, owns guns, and voted for Wisconsin’s concealed carry law back in 2012. Michael Alfonso has no clue of Fred's position on the Second Amendment or how deep his conservationist roots go.
Here’s what’s really going on: Michael is happy to throw stones online, but he won’t show up when it’s time to face voters. He skipped public forums. He let anonymous Super PAC money speak for him. He even told Fred directly, “Fred Clark, I’d love to [debate]. You have my number.” Then, for almost two months, our team called and emailed. Nothing.
If you believe candidates should answer questions in public before they ask for your vote, will you chip in $25 today so we can keep calling this out and keep showing up in every corner of the 7th District?
Help us find Alfonso → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wheresalfonso?refcode=62026_EOQ_4]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wheresalfonso?refcode=62026_EOQ_4 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wheresalfonso?refcode=62026_EOQ_4]
Fred and Michael finally crossed paths at a dairy breakfast this past weekend. When Fred asked him about the silence from his team, all Michael could offer was a vague “maybe August” debate that his people would set up. That is not respect for the people of Northern Wisconsin. That is hiding.
Where Alfonso HAS shown up has been road tripping across the country with his father in-law Sean Duffy on a corporate and taxpayer funded road trip that drew wide condemnation and an ethics complaint. Meanwhile, folks in the Northwoods watch gas prices climb, hurting tourism and their own summer plans.
So today, our campaign is launching a new site: Where’sAlfonso.com [http://wheresalfonso.com] to track every debate invitation and every no-show. We’re asking folks across all 26 counties to help us keep an eye on him and keep the pressure on.
The farther we can share this, the stronger the pressure will be on Alfonso to finally keep his word. Be sure to follow the website for updates, and share with your friends and neighbors, as well as on social media, and, if you can chip in to help us get our message out, we would be grateful.
Join the search → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wheresalfonso?refcode=62026_EOQ_4]
Thank you for joining us!

Peter, The 4th of July is around the corner, and **Bill Spadea** has something to say about it. **We're LIVE! >> **[**Join this special session now**](https://xtz223.keap-link013.com/v2/click/7a5736341dea70a3dc0c33d50a4511d4/eJyNkNFqwkAQRf9lnoPprhtNAkVETAixFkq16IukZsXVuLvdTGqN5N9dq_ik4OvMmXO5cwTkMpOY5BDCH9aUtsEBw5dCCy5xoCRmy_8t9RhpEwcKIbexUZWG8Hj3-Aacx37Q8R3Ag-YW-fzoD9JkHC9GyTi1pM6MzXjO06X05hm-9ZMRNM1DMd8JHP5adwkhmoqfG-XCtsKJKSy_RtRl6Lq1UrtWVbobNyD-C6Me6ZKgp_f5K4sm89k7Zd8eW02pX8z2GOHmKyIq_qk7LWJDMq25zK8fSvnhEtWcAAj5a9Q=) Bill has an exclusive message for tonight's session that you're going to want to hear. The average American works until April just to pay their tax bill. Business owners (people who sacrificed, risked everything, and built something real) are handing over tens of thousands more than they legally have to every single year. * * *

On Tuesday morning, the U.S. Supreme Court delivered a 5-4 ruling upholding birthright citizenship. This ruling was a response to an **[executive order](https://substack.com/redirect/143d560a-7543-4891-b84d-b0dad22571b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** President Donald Trump signed on his first day back in office last January, as a way to protect the "priceless and profound gift" of U.S. citizenship. His administration argued in the order that "the Fourteenth Amendment has never been interpreted to extend citizenship universally to everyone born within the United States." **[Chief Justice John Roberts ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/ddb7d8de-b478-4b0f-a43b-7bd5926cb4a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** against Trump's interpretation, holding that the children of illegal immigrants or other "temporarily present" individuals are indeed "'subject to the jurisdiction' of the United States and are citizens at birth under the Fourteenth Amendment."
In his 90-page dissent, Justice Clarence Thomas defended the Fourteenth Amendment as a way to secure equal citizenship for freed slaves in the post-Civil War era. However, he points out how subsequent SCOTUS decisions had undermined that intent to "selectively enforce" a supposedly colorblind constitution. "The Court has repurposed the Fourteenth Amendment to protect its own set of preferred rights that the Reconstruction Congress never contemplated and that cannot find support in its text," wrote Thomas. His dissent also acknowledged how the exploitation of the Fourteenth Amendment has been used to justify the growing practice of foreign birth tourists and illegal aliens having anchor babies in American soil. Justice Thomas concluded with the statement that "Today's opinion devalues... citizenship."

About **[4.4 million](https://substack.com/redirect/eacc1350-1cc7-486e-b91f-91a2e04953fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** U.S. born children under 18 live with a parent who is not an authorized U.S. citizen.

The number of illegal aliens in the United States has been steadily increasing for decades. 2022-2023 saw a record high number of U.S.-Mexico border encounters, with more than **[2.2 million](https://substack.com/redirect/27869fe0-b34d-4089-8e48-0c76887acae9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** per year. There were nearly 250,000 encounters in November of 2023 alone. Roughly 4 million illegal aliens currently in the U.S. are from Mexico, although this number has been **[declining](https://substack.com/redirect/f22103cb-e05f-4bfc-bb2d-1bc0931bf2a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Instead, the number of illegal aliens coming from other regions of the world grew from 5.8 million to 6.9 million between 2019 and 2022. Running for governor wasn't part of the plan when Susan and I moved to Colorado in 1997 as newlyweds. It was just the perfect place for us to build our new life together.
We packed our things into a U-Haul hitched to her station wagon and set out on our very own American Dream. Because back then, it was within reach.
**It's unacceptable to me that 30 years later, young folks have lost all hope of joining the middle class, buying a starter home and raising a family in our state** – the way we could at their age.
Throughout my career as a public servant, Coloradans have put their trust in me to fight for them in the U.S. Senate. I felt that responsibility deeply and still do.
I also knew that the best way to protect people struggling through a new Gilded Age – made worse by Trump's corruption – was to start here in our state.
That's why I couldn't sit out this race. And I'm confident we can win.
Since launching my campaign, thousands have joined our movement to make Colorado the best place to live, work and raise a family. I’m so grateful to count you among them.
But my opponent has made massive ad buys to crowd our vision off the airwaves. A super PAC funded by private equity and Big Oil and Gas bigwigs is also broadcasting lies about me to help him knock us out of the race.
**So if I'm going to get to work on Day One bringing the American Dream back within reach in Colorado as our next governor, I need your help to keep up our momentum and secure the Democratic nomination**.

# It's the end of the quarter -- so what!

Peter,Tonight at midnight, the fundraising quarter slams shut.
Now I know your inbox is about to get hammered by a hundred campaigns hollering that the sky is falling and the republic ends at 11:59pm if you do not give right this second.
We are not going to do that to you.
That is not how we operate, and you deserve better than to get scared into chipping in.
So here is the straight talk instead:
We do not have a billionaire sugar daddy.
We do not have a super PAC running cover for us.
What we have is a whole lot of regular folks scattered across the north woods, the river towns, and the dairy country who have decided this district is worth fighting for.
YOU are the entire operation.

| | Dear Friend,
---
| | This is not an easy email for me to write. I have always been a private person. Throughout my career, I have preferred talking about the people I represent, the challenges facing our communities, and the work that needs to be done—not about myself. But you deserve an explanation for my absence. Several months ago, due to health concerns, I entered the hospital for some testing. I believed I would be there for only a short time. Instead, I was given a diagnosis of depression. Depression is often misunderstood. Many people think it simply means feeling sad. But depression is so much more than that. The reality is that it affects every part of your life—physically, emotionally, and mentally. Until you experience it yourself, it is difficult to understand just how powerful this illness can be. My doctors recommended that I remain in the hospital and explained it would be the fastest way to recovery. To be honest with you, I was hesitant. Like so many people, I believed I could simply push through. I had responsibilities to my family, to New Jersey, and to the work I was elected to do. But I listened to my doctors. What I thought would be a matter of weeks became months. There is no set timeline for recovering from depression. There is only the work of getting better, one day at a time. Today, I am grateful that I accepted help. I am grateful for the incredible doctors, nurses, and caregivers who guided my recovery. Most importantly, **I am grateful to be back—healthier, stronger, and ready to continue fighting for the people of New Jersey.** This experience has also given me a much deeper appreciation for the millions of Americans and their families who quietly face similar struggles every day. To anyone carrying that burden, I hope you hear this: Asking for help is not weakness. It is strength. I also want to thank my family, whose love, faith, and unwavering support carried me through some of the hardest days of my life. Finally, to you—thank you. Thank you for your patience, for your understanding, and for your prayers. **I am excited to return to the work ahead, and I remain as committed as ever to fighting for the people of New Jersey's Seventh District.** **Our district remains one of the most competitive in the entire nation. Millions of dollars have already been pouring in against me, and millions more are on the way. ** [**If you are able, please consider supporting my re-election campaign so we have the resources we need to fight back and win.**](https://link.tomkean.com/s/c/ZayzGfT5NiPza6my4v0PfaAlRE_mFo0Nm3O0X3AVle0ps_DYsqPqLCfZSRSj3qPzZmhkaRWSiCfHC4M1BpRrw4u1XsLENoQpH_9E_MiA90d55UE7DYbNNJr7-CHHw_r7gfRjSykYB4a6vZKQ9oKoxRt3XVe2Ii2stTPjUu56b-f4RjcB5RXyKei7g_gGyqO_SaiWmLp13u6PbwZ5HRBE5OlTh-DVHuo2VwOaN4GNFO-u9DeZWJb33D2VDHJ5RfnxP0ZJ7ETkwRzI90X-BGFqohdQnvpnXCngC2bQ-Eih9gIMjVt-2N6ztkOxDuaLc8xLQ8WWbibPYekPYVBaFA4SYRmQH7KSGEGDh8L2OU51kQTEgVb_TDm84IfE6wu1tyL20GXIsZzeZbfF5zR2NfW2ZbnfqOjGlb-pn6xK2zK2Ko8LPSxNfposWM7K0WPaLPpsupSCaiK1R26hHN0HCnSqd6ldf3dinV9yziXuWlyOWnO2xTnUQ0Ak4iwNe8y6DH0SDxt-JeaBHjufc2AOSmHtObJdC5baeR_rKlz54oilnLpoolEu8UqYHz7-n3swsAfsom8EXUchqUDiNHyJFg04CfcUxAeP64o9Z8L5XLEpGz5Kl-U2UT8MmAsBNpV5s_MH4x-gdWbBNmYL71fkyQbMsMiE2fy7es3eH3pvueWy4g/yBJ0vXjjzDj8H9UdL98kVj68D_v6wLml/22)

clean_body: Our voice in Congress is needed now more than ever. | | | Friend, I can still fight against this fascist government and Trump and still deliver for our communities. Included in the recent bipartisan housing bill that has passed the House and Senate and will soon become law, is my Housing Our Communities Act, which will help local communities access HUD grants and capacity support so we can build affordable housing for all. Also this month, thanks to massive public outcry and nationwide grassroots support of my Ban Warehouse Detention Act, the Trump administration is backing off its plan to expand ICE detention centers into warehouses across the country —including the one they had planned to force on the city of Romulus in the congressional district next to mine. We’re making critical progress, but there is so much more work to do. Trump recently appointed a former executive from private prison corporation GEO Group to be the new acting director of ICE. We’ll keep fighting back against ICE’s terror campaign and detention centers’ inhumane conditions, while continuing to demand Congress abolish ICE and expand pathways to citizenship. In order to continue fighting for our communities, our rights, economic and environmental justice, and policies that put our household needs over corporate greed, I need your support. Tonight at midnight we’ll hit a critical fundraising deadline. After today, we’ll report to the Federal Election Commission how much we’ve raised and spent, and how much cash-on-hand we have for the fight ahead. body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Today is a big day—a big day for campaigns, as I am sure your inbox won’t let you forget. But it’s not just because it’s the end of the quarter and another reporting deadline–we also just got the final opinions from the Supreme Court for this term. And, rather than uphold limitations on money in politics and limiting coordination between parties and campaigns, today’s opinion removes them.
I’m still processing it all, as are people across town and across the country. And the other opinions out today, and in recent days. On birthright citizenship, affirmation from the Court—well, six of the justices—that the Constitution says what we can all read plainly. People born in the United States are citizens. That is a choice American citizens made generations ago, amending the Constitution to guarantee it. It is also a rejection of the President’s effort to remake our system of government with the stroke of his pen. On mail-in ballots, upholding a Mississippi law that allows that state to count ballots that are postmarked by election day but received later, protecting mail-in balloting there and in about more than two dozen states.
Unfortunately, other decisions this week provide more power to the president and strike at the heart of independence of government agencies and continuity of government. It’s all a lot.
And that’s just what’s happening across the street at the Supreme Court. There is plenty of drama happening in the House, and once again, it’s not clear. What is clear is that this House—this 119th Congress—is a rubber stamp for the Trump administration and its worst impulses.
It reminds us why the work we do matters so much. Our efforts to win this seat, hold it, and help other candidates and campaigns win, to take back the House majority, and to elect Democrats in Texas and beyond are absolutely critical now.
And we can’t do it without you. Today is a fundraising deadline day, and we know that the funds to deliver the messages to voters will be needed now more than ever in light of the Supreme Court decision and the redistricting
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260630?refcode=lpfe260630]
Every day gives each of us the opportunity to do more. Whether it’s clicking the link, signing up for a volunteer shift, or sharing information with your friends and family, all of us working together can do big things. Important things. Necessary things.
We’ve done it before. We can do it again. Thank you for being a part of this effort.
Together, we can do anything

| Peter,

I know I’ve said it before, but I truly want to thank you for trusting me to be your chosen Democratic Nominee for Maryland’s 6th District.

With that type of trust comes great responsibility.

Which is why even as Primary Day got closer and closer, I was still spending my time taking the concerns of our District and voicing them within Congress.

I was still working on making life more affordable for our families. – the same families that have nights where they don’t know if they’ll be able to put food on the table.

I was still fighting against Trump’s attempts to make his presidency about him instead of about everyday Americans.

_But that means that I don’t have as much time to personally focus on fundraising._

That’s why I wanted to ask you one last time this month**– Will you chip in $10 to my campaign so I can keep my focus on fighting to make a better life for those in Maryland without letting the Republicans outraise us?**

John and his wife Mikey call Bismarck home. He's fighting every day to keep North Dakota strong and America first.

_**by David Shuster**_
If there is a spectacle more pathetic than a political rally after the music and sound system have been packed away, it is a state fair in which the main exhibit is empty grass and pavement. The Great American State Fair, that grandiose Trump contrivance erected on the national mall, promised our nation an epic 250th birthday jubilee. Instead, it resembles something closer to an overfunded church picnic in the rain.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Endless photographs show long expanses of empty space, underwhelming attractions, logistical mishaps (including power outages that caused ice cream to melt,) and the unmistakable sensation that one had arrived hours after everyone else had gone home.
Donald Trump has always mistaken magnitude for greatness. If something is worth building, it must be colossal. If it is worth announcing, it must be historic. If it is worth remembering, it must be accompanied by adjectives swollen with self-regard including "greatest ever," and "unlike anything ever seen before."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So, Trump produced not just a fair, but a "Great American Fair," a title with enough letters to found an empire but not enough to hide an epic flop.
And the flops have been impossible to ignore. The Ferris wheel, which stopped working for several hours because of an electricity failure, now revolves with the lonely dignity of a courthouse ceiling fan. There is no line for that attraction.
And there are almost no people for most of the exhibits. The crowds have been so sparse that several state workers have simply abandoned their exhibits all together.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Musicians performing on the concert stage keep singing and strumming their MAGA greatest hits. But the other day, in the middle of the afternoon, there were only a dozen spectators.
And it was only a dozen if you count the four people who happened to be walking by, likely heading to their cars or the DC metro or an on-line game of solitaire.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In other words, the Fair has become a patriotic extravaganza in which the loudest applause is reserved for the sound of folding chairs being stacked at the end of each day.
There is an upside to all of this. It reinforces our nation's democratic genius. Most fairs ask visitors to marvel at prize pumpkins, blue-ribbon cattle, or improbable butter sculptures. This one has managed to elevate absence itself into an attraction.
Here is the Empty Promenade.
There is the deserted food court.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Observe, the Rare and Elusive Crowd, sighted only briefly before retreating to the permanent Smithsonian museums. At least the Smithsonian is interesting and informative.
Naturally, none of this will dent the Trump mythology. Reality never stands a chance against Trumpian math. A gathering of hundreds becomes thousands. Thousands become tens of thousands. Before the week expires, expect to hear that that every American family attended twice, and several unborn generations sent regrets.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The saddest feature of the Trump affair is not its meager attendance but its astonishing failure of imagination. America possesses genuine wonders: county fairs where livestock are more impressive and have more dignity than politicians; Midwestern festivals that smell gloriously of fried dough and fresh hay; carnivals where barkers are at least candid enough to admit they are selling illusion. Those entertainments merely ask members of the public to enjoy themselves.
This production asks the public to admire the producer Donald Trump. That is the essential defect. Patriotism cannot be manufactured by branding. And branding is both boring and uninspiring. Even the police have found themselves with so little to do, they have joined the cornhole toss games.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
National affection cannot be summoned by draping every available surface in red, white, and blue bunting while placing Trump's political personality at the center of every tableau. The Republic is older than any president and will, with luck, outlast every attempt to convert the annual July 4th birthday celebration into a testimonial dinner.
The truly comic aspect is that the National Mall has hosted crowds that altered the course of history, yet this latest extravaganza struggles to persuade joggers, bicyclists, and museum goers to interrupt their stroll. One can almost hear the ghosts of great assemblies whispering across the grass, wondering how a celebration of two and a half centuries of American vitality came to resemble the final clearance sale at a bankrupt drug store.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a85ffe-51e9-495a-80e8-ce826a9bd192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every carnival leaves behind wrappers, footprints, and fading music. This one may leave something rarer: the cautionary tale of America under Trump. We have a President who believes that self-advertisement and national celebration are interchangeable.
The midway on the National mall has delivered its own unmistakable verdict. The stark images possess a brutal eloquence. The showman, Donald Trump, expected a Great American State Fair triumph. But the audience found something better to do.

Melted ice cream, a stalled Ferris wheel, and a dozen spectators--inside the saddest party in America. | | and | Jun 30 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- by David Shuster If there is a spectacle more pathetic than a political rally after the music and sound system have been packed away, it is a state fair in which the main exhibit is empty grass and pavement. The Great American State Fair, that grandiose Trump contrivance erected on the national mall, promised our nation an epic 250th birthday jubilee. Instead, it resembles something closer to an overfunded church picnic in the rain. | | ---|---|--- Endless photographs show long expanses of empty space, underwhelming attractions, logistical mishaps (including power outages that caused ice cream to melt,) and the unmistakable sensation that one had arrived hours after everyone else had gone home. Donald Trump has always mistaken magnitude for greatness. If something is worth building, it must be colossal. If it is worth announcing, it must be historic. If it is worth remembering, it must be accompanied by adjectives swollen with self-regard including "greatest ever," and "unlike anything ever seen before." | | ---|---|--- So, Trump produced not just a fair, but a "Great American Fair," a title with enough letters to found an empire but not enough to hide an epic flop. And the flops have been impossible to ignore. The Ferris wheel, which stopped working for several hours because of an electricity failure, now revolves with the lonely dignity of a courthouse ceiling fan. There is no line for that attraction. And there are almost no people for most of the exhibits. The crowds have been so sparse that several state workers have simply abandoned their exhibits all together. | | ---|---|--- Musicians performing on the concert stage keep singing and strumming their MAGA greatest hits. But the other day, in the middle of the afternoon, there were only a dozen spectators. And it was only a dozen if you count the four people who happened to be walking by, likely heading to their cars or the DC metro or an on-line game of solitaire. | | ---|---|--- In other words, the Fair has become a patriotic extravaganza in which the loudest applause is reserved for the sound of folding chairs being stacked at the end of each day. There is an upside to all of this. It reinforces our nation's democratic genius. Most fairs ask visitors to marvel at prize pumpkins, blue-ribbon cattle, or improbable butter sculptures. This one has managed to elevate absence itself into an attraction. Here is the Empty Promenade. There is the deserted food court. | | ---|---|--- Observe, the Rare and Elusive Crowd, sighted only briefly before retreating to the permanent Smithsonian museums. At least the Smithsonian is interesting and informative. Naturally, none of this will dent the Trump mythology. Reality never stands a chance against Trumpian math. A gathering of hundreds becomes thousands. Thousands become tens of thousands. Before the week expires, expect to hear that that every American family attended twice, and several unborn generations sent regrets. | | ---|---|--- The saddest feature of the Trump affair is not its meager attendance but its astonishing failure of imagination. America possesses genuine wonders: county fairs where livestock are more impressive and have more dignity than politicians; Midwestern festivals that smell gloriously of fried dough and fresh hay; carnivals where barkers are at least candid enough to admit they are selling illusion. Those entertainments merely ask members of the public to enjoy themselves. This production asks the public to admire the producer Donald Trump. That is the essential defect. Patriotism cannot be manufactured by branding. And branding is both boring and uninspiring. Even the police have found themselves with so little to do, they have joined the cornhole toss games. | | ---|---|--- National affection cannot be summoned by draping every available surface in red, white, and blue bunting while placing Trump's political personality at the center of every tableau. The Republic is older than any president and will, with luck, outlast every attempt to convert the annual July 4th birthday celebration into a testimonial dinner. The truly comic aspect is that the National Mall has hosted crowds that altered the course of history, yet this latest extravaganza struggles to persuade joggers, bicyclists, and museum goers to interrupt their stroll. One can almost hear the ghosts of great assemblies whispering across the grass, wondering how a celebration of two and a half centuries of American vitality came to resemble the final clearance sale at a bankrupt drug store. | | ---|---|--- Every carnival leaves behind wrappers, footprints, and fading music. This one may leave something rarer: the cautionary tale of America under Trump. We have a President who believes that self-advertisement and national celebration are interchangeable. The midway on the National mall has delivered its own unmistakable verdict. The stark images possess a brutal eloquence. The showman, Donald Trump, expected a Great American State Fair triumph. But the audience found something better to do. Cliff 's Note: Trump spent a fortune to throw himself a 250th-birthday party on the National Mall. Nobody came. We can't fake an audience--and we don't have to. You're it. So here are two ways to plant your flag with Blue Amp before the bunting comes down: Founders: 250 for 250. | | ---|---|--- America turns 250 this year. . Your name on the wall, our gratitude on the record, and skin in the only celebration worth funding. Or: $36 for the whole year--through July 5th only. | | ---|---|--- That's the annual rate, two months free, locked in. The discount folds up when the fireworks do. After July 5th, it's gone. Empty grass and melted ice cream over there. A real audience over here. Come stand with the crowd that actually showed up. name: Dylan for Wisconsin
subject: Campaigning is a lot of work. But Wisconsin is more than worth it.
body:
The donations we get up to midnight tonight are our biggest chance for success for the final stretch before the primary.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/28797596abc7/c2y1sg9w12-10123134?e=f59034ca3e)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/WMgnrMdCTVv?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| | | | | | Hi Peter,
Today I am making fundraising calls, recording videos for our social media, and stapling yard signs with my team. Tonight's deadline determines the resources we have to get to the primary, but I also know how hard me, my team, and all of you who are supporting this campaign have worked.
I know we are capable of making it to the August primary, to the November election, and then getting down to the real work of bringing transparency and accountability back to Wisconsin. But I cannot do it alone.

---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/3LzLHlIKA_M?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| |
The Treasurers race is small compared to other state offices, but I have not let that stop me from working nonstop to get to as many parts of Wisconsin as I can, meeting as many people as I can, and modeling the transparency I will bring through my social media videos and speeches across the state.
Campaigning is not always glamorous, but tonight when we are knee-deep in yard signs, I know that I will not want to be anywhere else, because I believe in Wisconsin, and I believe in this work.. And I want to be able to keep doing it.
---
|
---
| | [**Today is a big deal for our campaign. The donations we get up to midnight tonight are our biggest chance for success for the final stretch before the primary. If you’re able, please donate $15, $25 (or if you’re able!) more to help us get to the primary in August.**](https://us.list-manage.com/110v_O2rD2K?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
Connect on social media with me if you want to see the videos I am working on, and all the places I travel, - [Facebook](https://us.list-manage.com/k3R59XV5UOe?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09), [Instagram](https://us.list-manage.com/UYwMGYWmOoW?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09), [TikTok](https://us.list-manage.com/fghI27QFOtF?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)!
Thank you...Dylan

## Hope & Action Turn Fear Into Freedom
One of the most patriotic things we can do is create climate hope and freedom. How? Find out by signing up for a free subscription to the [Climate Hope Together](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3MzUyODAwNjQ3LFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiMzg0ODVjY2NkMWIwNzQwOSJ9) Substack where we turn fear into freedom.

## What Is Substack?
Substack in an Internet communications platform that can include emails, a website with a blog, podcasts, and videocasts.

## What is a Subscription to Substack?
By signing up you will receive regular emails with new content.

## What is Climate Hope Together?
A Substack devoted to why there is still hope to overcome climate change. But we must join together to make hope happen. We are the hope we’ve been waiting for. We are climate hope together. (To find out more about me, go [here](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3MzY0MzM0OTg2LFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiOGE3NWU2MDdhYmI5ZGZhZSJ9).)
## What is on the Climate Hope Together Website?
On the Climate Hope Together [website](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3Mzc2OTE3OTAwLFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiMmVhMTI4ZjhkYmVjNDg5ZCJ9) you will find a variety of Series to explore.
* The [Intro Series](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3Mzg3NDAzNjYyLFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiMzIzZTgxMTRkNDk2M2I2NyJ9) provides an overview and introduction.
* [Olympian Fields of Action](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3Mzk3ODg5NDI0LFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiNDRmNzkzZGQ4OGM2ZmIyOSJ9) traverses the ways the Climate Movement can engage, utilizing the Olympics as the major metaphor.
* [Hope & Justice](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3NDA4Mzc1MTg3LFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiZjE3NTZhYzg0MGRiNDFiZiJ9) explores the deep connection between them.
* [Our Story Together](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3NDE3ODEyMzczLFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiY2JhMzVkMTUzMmI1YTc1NSJ9) narrates our past, spotlights Climate Action Heroes, and paints a picture of what we can be together.
* _[The Catalytic-4](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3NDI5MzQ2NzEyLFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiMThhYmRkYmMwMjNkMWM2ZiJ9)_ discusses the Four Catalytic Sources of Transformation through which we will prevail.
* [First Takes](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3NDQwODgxMDUwLFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiZmMzMGI3NWMzOGNmNTY0NiJ9) offers hot takes on what’s happening with the climate challenge.
* [Our Values](https://vvjoamr.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjE5MTgzMTYsXCJsXCI6MTkxNzM1NDg3NDUxMzY2ODEzLFwiclwiOjE5MTczNTQ5OTkwMzIwNzIwMH0iLCJzIjoiOTA2ZDg0ZTJmOTgwZDcwZSJ9) explores our Ten Movement Values: love, justice, beauty, creativity, freedom, wisdom, pragmatism, non-violence, sustainability, and success.

Together we are hope-makers, justice-achievers, and beauty-creators. We are the hope we’ve been waiting for. Our hope together overcomes climate fear and transforms it into climate freedom.

name: True the Vote
subject: The court rulings didn't close this door — but it shuts THIS THURSDAY! Have your voice heard!
body:
June 30, 2026 | Read Online ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/75u5p94oe7f8h6ro9eduzhw402633hnhrm7wg/x0hph6hev99nnnc5hl/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2Ivcjh1OGhvaDNnMG1wa3U0OG5uZzgzc2QwMnA2NjVhN2h4b3JwMg== )

Hi Friend —

This has been a hard week for those of us who care about election integrity, particularly as it relates to mail-in ballots. But there's an opportunity to have our voices heard — a United States Postal Service call for public comment that ends this Thursday, July 2.

Quick background:
-----------------

First, in the courts. Two rulings landed in the past week, and neither went our way.

On June 25, a federal judge in Massachusetts ruled in a case brought by 23 states and the District of Columbia. She struck down the President's March 2026 executive order on mail-in ballots as it applies to those states, and she went further, questioning whether the Postal Service even has the authority to set binding rules on how mail-in ballots are handled.

Then on June 29, the Supreme Court decided Watson v. RNC. By a 5-4 vote, with Justice Barrett writing for the majority, the Court held that states may continue counting mail-in ballots that are postmarked by Election Day even if they arrive afterward. You might wonder, if the ballot has to be postmarked by Election Day, isn’t that good enough? It might be if there were reliable procedural controls inside of election processes, but the fact is that as long as ballots continue to be counted, they will all be counted. Postmarks won’t be a limiting factor. That’s the real world.

So, that's the scoreboard. Two losses in one week.

But — the Postal Service has a separate, still-open rulemaking process in play. USPS is accepting public comments on a proposed rule to set uniform standards for mailing ballots in federal elections ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/75u5p94oe7f8h6ro9eduzhw402633hnhrm7wg/6qheh8hl8nnpp7iohk/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZmVkZXJhbHJlZ2lzdGVyLmdvdi9kb2N1bWVudHMvMjAyNi8wNi8wMi8yMDI2LTEwOTY4L2JhbGxvdC1tYWlsLWZvci1mZWRlcmFsLWVsZWN0aW9ucyNhZGRyZXNzZXM= ), with the official Election Mail logo on ballot envelopes, Intelligent Mail barcodes so ballots can be tracked through the system, and a reconciliation process so the number of ballots returned can be checked against the number sent. This rule making is its own legal process. The agency is required by law to read and weigh the public comments it receives before it decides anything. Note: the Massachusetts Federal Judge has questioned whether USPS has the authority to do this. That fight has yet to play out.

The comment period runs until July 2nd, nationwide, and is open to every American regardless of which state they live in.

Make no mistake, the other side of this argument is showing up. The League of Women Voters, Democracy Docket, and others have built tools to flood the docket with opposition. They are organized and after a week of wins, they are energized. We have until Thursday to make sure our voices are heard.

At this point, the only way to submit is by email. Send your comment to:

PCFederalRegister@usps.gov ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/75u5p94oe7f8h6ro9eduzhw402633hnhrm7wg/kkhmh6hn06688ntlh7/bWFpbHRvOlBDRmVkZXJhbFJlZ2lzdGVyQHVzcHMuZ292 )

Use the exact subject line: Ballot Mail

You must include your full name and mailing address in the body of the email, or USPS will not accept your comment. Your address won't be posted publicly, but the agency requires it to count your submission.

The deadline is Thursday, July 2, at 5:00 PM Eastern.

A few pointers to make your comment count: Write in your own words. Agencies note form letters but give real weight to genuine, personal comments. Three or four honest sentences will do more than any template. Be specific and be civil. Say who you are and why ballot transparency matters to you. If you've ever mailed a ballot and wondered whether it actually arrived, say so. That uncertainty is exactly what tracking and reconciliation are meant to fix. Keep it short. You do not need to write an essay. If it helps to have a starting point, here is a simple frame you can build on. Paste it into your email and add a sentence or two of your own:

"I am writing in support of the proposed rule, Ballot Mail for Federal Elections. As a voter, I want confidence that every ballot sent by mail can be tracked and accounted for. These standards bring basic transparency and a clear chain of custody to a process that has had too little of either. I urge the Postal Service to finalize the rule.”

[Your name]
[Your mailing address]

One housekeeping note: everything submitted becomes part of the public record, so don't include anything beyond the name and address USPS requires that you wouldn't want posted online.

Please take five minutes today and send in a comment. Be heard. Keep the faith. Never quit.

Ever onward —

I’ll be honest — I’m concerned.
With our end-of-quarter deadline just hours away, donations have slowed down at exactly the wrong time. It’s a moment when President Trump and his allies are ramping up their attacks on our democracy. And they are looking for any weakness to exploit.
They’re trying to restrict access to the ballot. They’re spreading lies about our elections. And they’re laying the groundwork to interfere in our democracy.
They want election officials who will look the other way. They want to intimidate us and hope we give up the fight. But that’s not who I am — and it never will be.
I’ve spent my career standing up for transparency, accountability, and the rule of law. As Secretary of State, I’ve continued that work by protecting our elections from political pressure and ensuring every vote is counted and Oregon’s elections continue to be the gold standard for accessibility and security. So I have to ask: Can you step up before midnight and help us close the gap? At this moment, we need to show the Trump Administration that we won’t be bullied. But if we hit our goal, we show that people are ready to stand up, speak out, and defend our democracy. I’m counting on you. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]

body:
The Supreme Court just announced its final rulings of June. They’re as bad as we thought. | |
---
Peter, **🚨BREAKING: The Supreme Court just announced its final rulings of June. One attacks the rights of trans kids. The other opens our democracy to even more billionaire money.** **And the last one was just one vote away from ending one of the most basic constitutional rights in the country—birthright citizenship.** Court-watchers expected this one to be a slam dunk. Instead it was a slim majority. The cases we’ve been waiting for all month have finally been decided. The rulings are just as bad as we thought they would be—if not worse. **The Roberts Court has been transformed into a political machine. It’s not looking out for We the People—it’s representing the extremist elites pulling the strings in the background.** [**We need Congress to rein in the corrupt and captured Supreme Court—fast. Write to your members of Congress and demand a plan to unrig our system and bring power back to the people.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOax_Tb2bOJVOyFl36_-dfzE82mSDDG_VK0ftS9ZBBaT7JNTskSLiKSJsfuTK408JLQYRpHtG5H74bKY_eiHVxqJnXXJkhQKNGHTIzol5x-n1p5Scjr5ibjtrfUyGFJL12O9tgTJqou8BlOfLmrmh8FbaO2Vwv5hhvBPo3TsUzn892B67grb7BCvS4cEJ2Uh3r-Sx5luepSny3fLRUW5s0HrmAWzdoizT_e1fl9qStvDaNahWqEjBrMnbvgXRA2pvvR4v4-ec9Z9NnzM6H7yv1Da4A/4rx/_O09Bbr9Sn6BLDHgwFb-NQ/h0/h001.IoXbu_52lV3MCYNlsHkSpo8gZrEj4IUi0oORHYXvMg8) [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOax_Tb2bOJVOyFl36_-dfzE82mSDDG_VK0ftS9ZBBaT7JNTskSLiKSJsfuTK408JLQYRpHtG5H74bKY_eiHVxqJnXXJkhQKNGHTIzol5x-n1p6aCGPh8vObCkUg1ZsBUiXQgtsocWn8HfIRnWr87-f_aaDWL6N4rXw0zvCEFEROjuCN172abvLgEtv4pUqB_kR-fEtg1S9IhqXE6r9-Er2kCn37lIAm-SSYBWyNNe0RD2tZGyahcxFOTm_y4QNs30ny6Sjgf3VGoIayYILnmg_lPw/4rx/_O09Bbr9Sn6BLDHgwFb-NQ/h1/h001.a8e3np06UsbBI8LdGuaOIAEQATXOEWDCIRI0o_l-rPM) **In the first case, the Supreme Court upheld bans against trans kids playing sports with their friends.** They seized on the most politically charged, MAGA-coded culture war fight available and delivered exactly the outcome the far right wanted. **In the second case, the Court struck down limits on coordinated campaign spending.** The case essentially allows the wealthy and corporations to spend unlimited amounts in direct coordination with the candidates they support, warping our democracy and economy even further. **The campaign finance case the Court ruled on today directly affects the balance of power in this country.** It’s the single biggest gift this Court could hand to the wealthy donors and dark money interests who built its majority in the first place. The ruling will shape elections for a generation. Combined with the Court’s attack on voting rights in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , it amounts to directly stealing the voices of everyday people and handing their power to wealthy elites. We have a choice: We can continue down this road of increasingly extreme perversions of the constitution, or we can stand up for the country we grew up in. **We need a Supreme Court that is structurally reformed and genuinely accountable, not one that warps our system to serve the powerful. United for Democracy is leading the people-powered mass movement that will not stop demanding reform until it’s achieved.** [**Send a message to your member of Congress right now. Tell them to unrig the system and give power back to the people in the wake of the Court’s latest disastrous rulings.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOax_Tb2bOJVOyFl36_-dfzE82mSDDG_VK0ftS9ZBBaT7JNTskSLiKSJsfuTK408JLQYRpHtG5H74bKY_eiHVxqJnXXJkhQKNGHTIzol5x-n1p7E9M556B9rsizQBgXKgrXm-i8tj_WW0aZCdpVXzhNkrEtxqvDBizDUbFUnEHqPHfdyFHm1P74WzDwPoh_Z9xMi2fk0_RzzBXdT_B_u7uTITqCp-sOROpI5yCzjcufr8GdUB__-HwjtVcmpSeF_7cNgxM1kufBcMMbICnyMBV84RA/4rx/_O09Bbr9Sn6BLDHgwFb-NQ/h2/h001.SZhQkBgHtaLXe1t2Ysd9CqVU1d8iOAbs3OHyjXgIqq8) Thank you for responding quickly to today’s Supreme Court rulings, Morgan Stahr

Let that sink in: as families struggle with rising medical bills, more expensive groceries, and higher electricity bills, **Trump loves it.** That's the arrogance and callousness of a leader who would cut taxes for billionaires while gutting healthcare for working families. Who would start illegal wars that spike gas prices.
